-
-== Context
-
-Production use needs VS Code and JetBrains plugins with first-class DX. ADR-014 already decided that
-highlighting must derive from the engine lexer rather than a forked grammar, but it spoke to our
-in-process JS front-ends (the Lab's CodeMirror plugin, the tutorials' overlay). Real editors need a
-*delivery mechanism*, and that forces a sharper question than "which grammar format."
-
-The decisive constraint is that highlighting FlatBars is *stateful and content-dependent*:
-
-* *Set delimiters* (ADR-015): after `pass:[{{=<% %>=}}]` every later tag uses the new pair until
-  `pass:[<%={{ }}=%>]`. A correct highlighter must carry the *active delimiter pair* as state across the
-  document.
-* *Per-dialect grammar*: the `parseExpr` / `parseHead` seam and `LexOptions` make tag interiors and the
-  legal shape set differ across RawBars / FullBars / MaxBars / MinBars; the separator set that paints as
-  a statement is the parser's own `standaloneSeps` (empty for MinBars), never a fixed keyword list.

-  `pass:[{{<}}]` / `pass:[{{$}}]`.

-== Decision
-

-  as LSP semantic tokens.* A single language server (`flatbars-lsp`, Node, embedding the `flatbars-js`
-  bundle and its `tokenize(template, dialect)` API — the interior-aware superset of ADR-014's
-  `highlightSpans`) computes positioned token kinds for the
-  document — stateful by construction, so set delimiters, dialects, raw blocks and separators are all
-  correct because there is no second grammar to be wrong. Both VS Code (semantic-tokens LSP client) and
-  JetBrains (LSP API, 2023.2+) consume *the same server*; one implementation, all editors. (The JetBrains
-  platform LSP API has historically been Ultimate-only; Community-edition IDEs do not attach the server
-  and see only the TextMate fallback below — which is exactly why that fallback is mandatory, not a reason
-  against the LSP.) The server is
-  also the substrate for the rest of DX — diagnostics from the recovering parser
-  (xref:adr-0023-recovering-parser.adoc[ADR-023]: ONE parser that recovers, of which the canonical
-  fail-fast `parse` is a projection — not a second engine), helper hover/completion from `preludeSchema`
-  and the catalog, and go-to-partial. Highlighting was the first feature on this substrate, needing *none*
-  of the recovering parser, so it shipped first; diagnostics followed once ADR-023 landed.
-
-. *A shared `flatbars.tmLanguage.json` is a mandatory, committed fallback — not optional.* Every plugin
-  ships it. The LSP is not always present or instant, and some contexts have *no* language server at
-  all, where the TextMate grammar is the only highlighting the user ever sees:
-+
---
-* first paint, before the server activates / attaches;
-* environments with no LSP: code review on GitHub/Gitea, diffs, `bat`/`less`/`cat` previews, marketplace
-  screenshots, documentation code blocks;
-* JetBrains' TextMate-bundle path for files before (or without) the plugin;
-* a degraded/crashed or still-starting server — DX must never fall to *no* colour.
---
-+
-Because those contexts are real and unavoidable, shipping the grammar is non-negotiable. We use the
-*well-known Handlebars TextMate grammar*, re-identified as `source.flatbars` and extended for all four
-dialects (inverse sections, Mustache inheritance `pass:[{{<}}]`/`pass:[{{$}}]`, set delimiters, and

-non-authoritative*: being stateless it cannot follow a
-set-delimiter *switch* (the tags past `pass:[{{=A B=}}]`) and is FullBars-flavoured (it paints
-`else`/`each` as keywords even in MinBars, and paints RawBars/MaxBars's `extras`-off shapes as valid).

-the floor is now a rich, familiar grammar, the LSP emits a token ONLY where it knows something the
-stateless grammar cannot — dialect-scoped interior operators/literals, set delimiters, and
-dialect-disallowed errors (the vocabulary's `lspEmitKinds`). The structural tags (interpolation, raw,
-blocks, partials, comments) are left to the grammar, so `pass:[{{{x}}}]` keeps its braces-vs-name colour
-instead of being flattened to one whole-tag semantic token. The grammar is the floor; the engine is the
-ceiling *only where the engine knows more*.
-
-. *The fallback is a derived artifact and MUST be drift-bounded, like every other.* But it is *richer*
-  than the engine — it splits a tag into sigil / name / args / literals, where the engine paints one kind
-  per tag (ADR-014) — so a scope-to-kind bijection does not fit, and we do not force one. `check:tmgrammar`
-  instead pins, *for each dialect*, the one thing the engine defines and a stateless grammar can be held
-  to: *tag boundaries* — exactly the characters the engine marks as inside a FlatBars tag are the
-  characters the grammar scopes as a tag (every tag scope ends in `.flatbars`; host text and the YAML
-  front-matter block never do), which catches the Exhibit-A/B begin/end drift across all four dialects.

-  the LSP, which corrects them as semantic tokens over the silent floor.) Everything

-  contexts forever), so its gate is permanent too. The token vocabulary (`editors/token-vocabulary.json`)
-  is still the one place the kinds, the LSP legend, and the grammar's literal scopes are defined together.
-
-. *Reject tree-sitter as the FlatBars parser/highlighter.* A tree-sitter grammar is a second source of
-  truth (the drift ADR-001 and ADR-014 exist to prevent); it cannot track the dialect seam without N
-  grammars; its statefulness requires a hand-written C external scanner duplicating set-delimiter logic;
-  and it is not JetBrains' highlighting path, so it would not unify editors. If Zed / Neovim / GitHub
-  tree-sitter highlighting later becomes a goal, a tree-sitter grammar may be added as *another
-  non-authoritative fallback* under the same drift gate — never as the engine's parser.
-
-. *Reject native per-editor lexers* (a JFlex/Kotlin lexer for JetBrains plus a separate VS Code

-  one source of truth, for no benefit the LSP does not already give.

-  industry pattern (TypeScript, rust-analyzer). At template sizes the semantic round-trip is
-  imperceptible.
-* *Two highlighting representations exist by design* (the engine and the TextMate fallback). Unlike the
-  drift ADR-014 fought, the authority is unambiguous (the engine always wins where it runs), and the
-  fallback is gated, scoped to default delimiters, and labelled — *bounded* drift, not silent drift.

-  colour per tag); the richer interior axis lives only in `tokenize`, which the editor layer consumes. The
-  TextMate grammar is for *external / no-LSP* contexts, not for our own front-ends.

-  and corrected the instant one attaches. That is the honest limit of any stateless fallback, and the
-  reason the fallback is a floor rather than the design.

-*Status:* Accepted. *Date:* 2026-06-02. Builds on
-xref:adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker.adoc[ADR-001] (helpers are the meaning plug-in) and
-xref:adr-0011-compile-to-js.adoc[ADR-011] (compile ≡ interpret). Extends the FullBars
-Handlebars-faithfulness claim (xref:fullbars-compat.adoc[]) from syntax/semantics to the one piece of the

-== Context

-A JS host can render and compile FullBars, but cannot supply its own helper:
-`Handlebars.registerHelper('loud', s => s.toUpperCase())` has no equivalent. Helpers are the IoC
-plug-in (ADR-001) — but the plug-in language has been PureScript (`Kernel.Prelude`), and the JS facade
-ships only that curated prelude. For real Handlebars users, registering a helper is the *single most
-common* extension, so "Handlebars-faithful" without it is faithful to the grammar and unfaithful to the

-
-. *Two execution modes.* FlatBars runs templates two ways and gates that they agree byte-for-byte
-  (`test:compile`, ADR-011). A user helper must work in *both* the interpreter and the compiled module,
-  or be explicitly mode-limited. The compiled runtime already has a closed helper registry
-  (`flatbars-runtime.mjs`: `const helpers = {…}` + `rt.call` → `UnknownHelper`); the interpreter
-  (PureScript) has an extensible env (`Kernel.Env.registerAll`) but *no* FFI to adopt a JS function as a
-  `Helper` over the `Value` type.
-. *Escaping.* The reference engine never auto-escapes raw output and escapes `Value` strings in
-  `pass:[{{ }}]`. A JS helper returns a string; that must land as an *escaped* `VString` in

-. *Validation.* Unknown helpers are a schema error (`Kernel.Walk`, `allowUnknown`) and a runtime
-  `UnknownHelper`. A registered helper must extend the schema or it is rejected before it runs.

-  types both template and helper into one page, and workspaces are shareable by URL: helper *source*
-  riding along in a link would let a shared link execute attacker JS in the victim's origin. FlatBars's
-  deliberate "no template `eval` / no render `policy`" stance is about *template* eval; host-registered
-  helpers are a different axis — but the Lab blurs host and template.

-== Decision
-
-. *User-defined helpers are inline-only, dual-mode, and escaped-by-default.* A host registers
-  `name → (args…) → value` functions; they are usable in both the interpreter and the compiled module,
-  and produce escaped output in `pass:[{{ }}]` unless the value is marked safe.
-
-. *One registration feeds both modes.* The facade marshals each JS helper into (a) a PureScript
-  `Helper` over `Value` (via an FFI call site) registered into the render env, and (b) the compiled
-  runtime registry (`rt.register`). Both paths therefore execute *the same* JS function with *the same*
-  marshalling, so `test:compile` stays byte-identical — and the equivalence is gated with custom-helper
-  cases.
-
-. *The marshalling contract.* Arguments marshal `Value → JS` (string/number/boolean/null/array/object);
-  surface hash args (`key=value`) arrive as a trailing plain-object argument (the engine already
-  desugars them to a dict). The return marshals `JS → Value`: a string ⇒ `VString` (escaped in
-  `pass:[{{ }}]`); `safe(string)` — a sentinel from the bundle's exported `safe` — ⇒ `VSafe` (raw),
-  the `SafeString` equivalent. A thrown JS error becomes a located render/compile error, never an
-  uncaught throw.
-
-. *Registered names extend the schema.* Helpers registered for a run are added to the validation schema
-  (known name, inline kind, `AnyArity` unless declared), so they neither trip "unknown helper" nor lose
-  the arity diagnostics the prelude gets.

-  `renderWith(helpers, partials, template, data)` (plus `safe`) — a helpers *bag* `{ name: fn }` passed
-  per call, with *no* global mutable registry (clean for tests and for a shared Lab). There is
-  deliberately *no* `compileWith`: compilation emits `rt.call(name, …)` for any non-built-in head

-= ADR-021: The MaxBars/RawBars variable model — `this` / `loop` / `root` / `parent` / `outer`
-:navtitle: ADR-021 MaxBars variable model
-
-*Status:* Proposed. *Date:* 2026-06-03. *Supersedes* xref:adr-0006-maxbars-loop-variables.adoc[ADR-006]
-Decision §1–2 (the bare loop-variable vocabulary) and §5 (its v1 outer-loop limit). *Extends*
-xref:adr-0013-labelled-loops.adoc[ADR-013] (labelled loops → `outer`). Applies to *MaxBars and RawBars*
-only; FullBars is unchanged (Handlebars-faithful).
-
-== Context
-
-Three things converged to make the loop/context vocabulary worth redesigning:
-
-* *ADR-006 bare loop variables* gave MaxBars `pass:[{{index0}}]`, `pass:[{{first}}]`, `pass:[{{length}}]`,
-  `pass:[{{key}}]`, … as *bare* scoped names. They silently shadow data fields — the schema-less
-  *warn-always* lint (`loopVarShadowWarnings`) exists *only* to paper over that footgun — and they reach
-  just the *current* loop.
-* *ADR-013 labelled loops* added `label NAME` → the loop frame reified as an object
-  (`pass:[{{outer.index1}}]`). It proved the mechanism: *a dotted head resolves against a binding only
-  when the name is scope-declared* (`pass:[{{c.deep.n}}]` works because `c` is a block param;
-  `pass:[{{root.title}}]` / `pass:[{{parent.title}}]` render *empty* because `root`/`parent` are frame
-  helpers but **not** scope-declared, so they parse as data paths).
-* *Reaching the enclosing / root context* still relied on Handlebars' `@root` and `pass:[../]` — the
-  `@` namespace the non-Handlebars dialects want to drop.
-
-The decision: replace the bare magic vocabulary with a small set of **reserved, namespaced, chainable**
-scoped names, and drop `@`/`pass:[../]` in MaxBars and RawBars.
-
-== Decision
-
-. *The model is `this` / `loop` / `root` / `parent` / `outer`* — five reserved scoped names, available in
-  *MaxBars and RawBars*. FullBars is untouched: it keeps `@index`/`@root`/`pass:[../]` (Handlebars
-  fidelity) and does *not* get these names. The set is *complete*: current context (`this`), current-loop
-  metadata (`loop`), a named enclosing loop's metadata (`outer`/labels), enclosing context (`parent`),
-  root context (`root`).
-
-. *Frames chain.* Every frame-shifting block (`each`, `with`) pushes a frame linked to its parent frame
-  and the root. The reserved names resolve against this chain, and **chain from day one**:
-+
-[cols="1,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Name |Resolves to
-
-|`this` |the current context (raw data). Unchanged.
-|`loop` |the *current loop's metadata object* (`each` only) — see the loop-object shape below. Chains
-  over enclosing *loops*: `pass:[{{loop.parent.index0}}]`, `pass:[{{loop.parent.parent.length}}]`,
-  `pass:[{{loop.root.length}}]`.
-|`outer` |a *named* enclosing loop's metadata object (any `label NAME`, ADR-013) — same shape as `loop`.
-|`parent` |the *enclosing context* object. Chains over enclosing *contexts*: `pass:[{{parent.name}}]`,
-  `pass:[{{parent.parent.name}}]`.
-|`root` |the *root context* object (outermost context).
-|===
-+
-`loop`/`outer` are *loop metadata* (chain over enclosing **loops**); `parent`/`root` are *contexts*
-(chain over enclosing **contexts**). They are complementary, not redundant: `pass:[{{loop.parent.index0}}]`
-is the enclosing loop's index; `pass:[{{parent.name}}]` is a field on the enclosing context.
-
-. *Object shapes (normative).*
-+
-* *loop-object* (`loop`, `outer`, any label): `{ index0, index1, rindex0, rindex1, first, last, length,
-  key, this, parent, root }`. The index/`first`/`last`/`length` arithmetic is ADR-006's (`rindex0 =
-  length − 1 − index0`, `first = index0 == 0`, …); `this` is the element; `parent` is the nearest
-  *enclosing loop*'s loop-object (or `null`); `root` is the *outermost loop*'s loop-object (or itself).
-  An **immutable per-iteration snapshot**.
-* *context-object* (`parent`, `root`): the context's *own* fields, plus the reserved links
-  `{ this, parent, root }` (reserved names win on collision). `parent` is the enclosing context-object
-  (or `null` at the top level); `root` is the root context-object.
-
-. *Reserved-name resolution (the mechanism).* The reserved names are **scope-declared** so a dotted head
-  resolves the binding, not a data path — the ADR-013 mechanism, generalized.
-+
-* *MaxBars* — the surface desugar **seeds** the reserved names into `scope` (so `pass:[{{loop.first}}]`
-  desugars to `(lookup (loop) "first")`, not a data lookup). This seeding is *MaxBars-only*: it rides the

-  MaxBars-only scoped-name seeding."
-* *RawBars* — has no surface desugar, so the names are reached as ordinary *operations* the frame
-  installs, in RawBars' explicit style: `pass:[{{{loop}}}]`, `pass:[{{{lookup loop "first"}}}]`,
-  `pass:[{{{lookup (lookup loop "parent") "index0"}}}]`.
-* The *engine* installs the same frame bindings for both dialects; FullBars' surface routes bare names to
-  data lookups, so it never reaches them — no gating of the bindings is required.
-

-  `@`-prefixed name or a `pass:[../]` run is a *located parse error* that points the author at `root` /
-  `parent` / `loop`. MaxBars-local; FullBars' default parser keeps both. RawBars never had `@`/`pass:[../]`
-  (no surface), so there is nothing to remove there.
-
-. *The bare loop-variable vocabulary is removed* (supersedes ADR-006 §1–2). MaxBars passes
-  `noLoopVars`, so bare `pass:[{{first}}]` / `pass:[{{index0}}]` / `pass:[{{length}}]` / `pass:[{{key}}]`
-  are ordinary *data fields*; their values live as fields of `loop`. The frame no longer installs the
-  standalone `index0`/`first`/… operations, so RawBars' `pass:[{{{index}}}]` / `pass:[{{{first}}}]` /
-  `pass:[{{{parent-index}}}]` are likewise replaced by `loop.*`.
-
-. *The block-partial body is the reserved name `yield`.* Handlebars' `pass:[{{> @partial-block}}]`
-  yield is unwritable in the non-Handlebars dialects — `@` is reserved (§5), and a bare `partial-block`
-  lexes as the subtraction `partial - block` under MaxBars' infix arithmetic. `yield` is added as a
-  hyphen-free *synonym* of the `partial-block` scoped operation, installed under both names in the
-  partial block frame, so the one yield is spelled `pass:[{{yield}}]` (MaxBars), `pass:[{{{yield}}}]`
-  (RawBars), and `pass:[{{> @partial-block}}]` (FullBars, unchanged). It is reserved like the other
-  roots: a same-named data field is shadowed (read it with an explicit `pass:[{{lookup this "yield"}}]`),
-  and a `pass:[label yield]` is flagged by the label-shadow lint. The yield is escape-safe (`VSafe`), so
-  MaxBars' `pass:[{{ }}]` form does not re-escape it.
-

-  field"; with the metadata behind `loop.`, the reserved roots are `this`/`loop`/`root`/`parent`/`outer`
-  (and `yield` inside a block partial) — explicit, and rarely data fields except `yield`, whose escape
-  hatch is the explicit lookup above. ADR-006's `loopVarShadowWarnings` is deleted. The
-  ADR-013 `labelShadowWarnings` (a `label NAME` colliding with a reserved root — `this`/`loop`/`root`/
-  `parent`/`yield`) stays; a lighter optional lint may warn when a data field named one of the roots is

-  `pass:[{{this.NAME}}]` (the path reduces to the segment `NAME`), so the explicit `lookup` is the only
-  field escape.
-
-. *Compiler parity.* The frame chain + reserved-name objects are emitted by the compiler exactly as the
-  interpreter builds them — the ADR-013 `rt.each`/`childFrame` `binds` chain extends to carry `loop` /
-  `parent` / `root` and the parent links — gated by `test:compile` (interpreter ≡ compiled).
-
-== Examples
-
-[source,handlebars]
-----
-{{!-- MaxBars --}}
-{{#each rows as |row| label outer}}
-  {{#each row.cells}}
-    {{loop.index1}}/{{loop.length}}       {{!-- this (inner) loop --}}
-    {{outer.index0}} of {{outer.length}}  {{!-- the named enclosing loop --}}
-    {{loop.parent.first}}                 {{!-- the enclosing loop, unnamed --}}
-    {{parent.heading}}                    {{!-- the enclosing context (a row) --}}
-    {{parent.parent.title}}               {{!-- two contexts up --}}
-    {{root.report.id}}                    {{!-- the root context --}}
-  {{/each}}
-{{/each}}
-----
-
-== Alternatives considered (team debate)
-
-* *Flat names, no chaining* (`loop`/`outer`/`parent`/`root` but no `parent.parent`/`loop.parent`) —
-  rejected: developers expect chaining from day one.
-* *Hierarchy only* (`this`/`loop`/`outer`, fold `root`/`parent` under `loop`) — rejected: `root`/`parent`
-  are not conceptually under `loop`, and the folding breaks in `pass:[{{#with}}]` bodies (no `loop`).
-* *Keep `@`/`pass:[../]` alongside the new names* — rejected: the goal is to *drop* `@` in the
-  non-Handlebars dialects; coexistence defeats it.
-* *MaxBars-only (exclude RawBars)* — rejected by requirement: the model is for both non-Handlebars
-  dialects. The asymmetry is only in *reach* (MaxBars: dotted paths via seeding; RawBars: explicit
-  operations), not in the underlying bindings.
-* *Keep the bare vocabulary for backward compatibility* — rejected: repo policy is no compat shims; the
-  bare vars become data fields and templates migrate (below).
-
-== Migration
-
-* *MaxBars:* bare `pass:[{{index0}}]`/`pass:[{{first}}]`/… → `pass:[{{loop.index0}}]`/`pass:[{{loop.first}}]`;
-  `pass:[{{@root.x}}]` → `pass:[{{root.x}}]`; `pass:[{{../x}}]` → `pass:[{{parent.x}}]`. Touches the
-  `mx:loopvars-*` conformance cases, the `loopVars`/`loopObject` tutorial examples, the MaxBars
-  interpreter `loopvars-*` tests, and `maxbars.adoc`.
-* *RawBars / core corpus:* `pass:[{{{index}}}]` / `pass:[{{{key}}}]` / `first` / `last` /
-  `pass:[{{{parent-index}}}]` (the `each-array`, `each-first-last`, `each-array-key-null`,

-  ADR-013; `nav.adoc` registration; `maxbars.adoc` and the RawBars page.
-* *Build:* regenerate the Lab bundle; `test:compile` and full `npm test` green.
-
-== Consequences
-
-* *Pro:* one coherent, chainable, namespaced model; the shadow footgun is essentially gone (metadata is
-  behind `loop.`); `@`/`pass:[../]` are dropped from the non-Handlebars dialects as intended; reuses the
-  ADR-013 frame mechanism.

-  block body — `yield` most notably, a common data field (bond/crop yield), whose only escape is the
-  explicit `pass:[{{lookup this "yield"}}]`; building the frame *chain* (`parent`/`root` links,
-  multi-level) is more engine/compiler work than ADR-013's single frame.
-
-== Open questions
-
-* Exact error text for `@` / `pass:[../]` in MaxBars (point at `root`/`parent`/`loop`).
-* `parent` at the *top level* (no enclosing context): propose `null`; `root` is always available.
-* Whether to expose `loop.depth` (nesting depth) — *defer* to a follow-up.

-appears in **zero** golden or vendored fixtures — only unit tests. A configuration surface with no users
-is paying a 24-file tax.
-
-*Portability is undecidable by inspection.* A template that renders on more than one engine ({hbs},
-Mustache, StringTemplate4, …) silently diverges whenever a condition tests one of the *ambiguous four* —
-`pass:[""]`, `0`, `pass:[[]]`, `pass:[{}]` — on which engines disagree. The divergence is invisible on the
-happy path; it surfaces only for the input whose value lands on an ambiguous shape, which is exactly the
-input the author's fixtures omit. FlatBars cannot flag it statically (no value types).

-Team review (debate recorded against this ADR) separated two questions the original instinct fused:
-*configurability* (the cost) from *representation* (a `Set` of shapes vs a lambda). The cost is the
-configurability; the representation is fine either way and a lambda interface is the right IoC shape *if*
-its implementations stay introspectable.

-== Part A — Decision: truthiness is a fixed per-engine lambda

-  shape interpret/desugar/validate/compile already use ("don't call FlatBars, FlatBars calls you").
-  FullBars plugs in the Handlebars rule; *RawBars and MaxBars plug in `nonEmpty`* (`false null "" [] {}`
-  falsy — `0` truthy, every empty container falsy; the dialects deliberately diverge in value policy since
-  RawBars/MaxBars are not Handlebars clones); MinBars plugs in the language-agnostic Mustache rule
-  (`mustache`: `false null []` falsy, `0`/`""`/`{}` truthy — the Ruby/Python implementations).
-  *There is no per-file
-  override* — the engine's rule is the only rule a template runs under, swapped in at the dialect's render
-  and compile entry points (interpreter via `withTruthy` for the FlatBars dialects, the `MinEnv.truthy`
-  field for MinBars; compiler via the seeded runtime callback).
-+
-[NOTE]
-S2 amendment — *MinBars `mustache.js`-compat mode.* The dominant JavaScript Mustache, `mustache.js`,
-does not follow the spec rule above: it skips a section on `!value`, so `0` and `""` are falsy there (and
-an empty list renders zero times), which is *identical to the `handlebars` rule*. `Kernel.Value` therefore
-defines `mustacheJs = handlebars` as a self-documenting alias, and MinBars exposes an opt-in compat path
-that seeds it instead of `mustache` — `renderMinbarsCompat` / `compileMinbarsCompat` in the JS facade,
-`renderMinCompat` in the engine, and `flatbars --mustache-js` on the CLI. The spec rule stays MinBars'
-default (so the 184/184 conformance is untouched); the compat path is for hosts porting a `mustache.js`
-codebase that need byte-for-byte section behaviour. The interpreter/compiler agreement on the compat rule
-is gated by the `minbars-compat` cases in the compile-conformance harness.
-
-. *The built-in rules are named `Value -> Boolean` predicates.* `Kernel.Value` keeps `handlebars`,
-  `nonEmpty`, `mustache` (the engine rules) plus `minimal`/`presence` (analyse comparison rules) as the
-  *menu* an engine selects from and what Part B replays for divergence. (Originally these were
-  `FalsySet`-derived data; a later step purged the falsy-set form entirely, so a rule is now *only* a
-  callback.) This is the synthesis the
-  debate reached: an *opaque* lambda was rejected (it can be neither baked nor reasoned about), and a
-  fixed lambda *backed by a named set* keeps every introspection the data form gave us.
-
-. *Delete the configuration surface.* Removed: the `@truthiness` *directive meaning*; `aliasSet`,
-  `resolveTruthiness`/`resolveTruthinessWith`/`parseTruthiness`, the shape-literal parser; `withFalsy`,
-  `RefEnv.partialFalsy`, `registerPartialsFalsy` and the cross-partial scoping rules; and the linter's
-  truthiness-*materialization* phase (it existed *only* to keep non-default modes render-exact — with no
-  non-default modes, MaxBars→RawBars lowering is render-exact for free). The core `Directive` carriage is
-  untouched — `@trim` still needs it, and a now-inert `@truthiness` is *carried, never an error*, but
-  `directiveLints` warns it as deprecated so a stale directive does not silently mislead.
-+
-*As-built note (compiler).* The plan said the compiler should drop the baked `$falsy` constant entirely.
-In practice the FullBars and MinBars compiled paths share one runtime (`flatbars-runtime.mjs`) but need
-*different* fixed rules (handlebars vs mustache), so ripping `$falsy` out would mean a rule table in the
-shared runtime — disproportionate risk for no behavioural gain. The implemented change keeps `$falsy` but
-bakes it as a **fixed per-dialect constant** (`resolveForCompile` ignores directives and returns the
-engine rule); the *per-file configurability* — the actual over-engineering — is gone, and
-`test:compile` stays byte-identical (296/296).
-
-. *`includeZero` survives, decoupled from the machinery.* It becomes a per-call helper option on
-  `if`/`unless` (`0` + `includeZero` ⇒ truthy), not a `FalsySet` mutation. It is genuine Handlebars
-  compat (the clone goal — xref:fullbars-compat.adoc[]); the 28 references simplify rather than vanish.
-
-. *An open (arbitrary host) truthiness lambda is rejected for now.* Letting a host pass any
-  `Value -> Boolean` (e.g. "the string `"no"` is falsy") is expressive but (a) *non-compilable* — the
-  emitter cannot serialise a host closure, so it would break compile ≡ interpret (ADR-011), and (b) makes
-  cross-engine portability *undecidable by inspection* (Part B could no longer replay a known menu). If it
-  ever ships it is interpreter-only and explicitly non-bakeable. Deferred.
-
-== Part B — Decision: analyse mode
-
-. *Analyse mode is an engine **variant**, not a second interpreter.* `Kernel.Analyse` builds the analysis
-  engine as the real prelude with the five truthiness operations — `if`/`unless`/`and`/`or`/`not` (the
-  only places `truthy` is consulted; MaxBars' `&&`/`||`/`!` desugar to them) — *wrapped*. Each wrapper
-  **delegates to the original operation** to produce output, then records a `Decision`. Output is
-  *byte-identical to a normal render by construction* — there is no second evaluator to drift from the
-  first (the discipline ADR-011 enforces between compiler and interpreter, applied here between analyser
-  and interpreter). An analyse run that reports zero findings is a *proof* that the render is
-  truthiness-portable against that data.
-
-. *The trace sink is a closure-captured `Ref`, not an env field.* The analysis entry point runs on the
-  existing `ExceptT Error Aff` path, creates a `Ref (Array Decision)`, and the five wrappers append via
-  `liftEffect`. `RefEnv` is **not** extended and the pure `Either` render path is **untouched**.

-. *A `Decision` is the closed record:*
-+
-[source]
-----
-{ span     :: Span     -- location of the enclosing tag (Ctl already carries it, "for diagnostics")
-, op       :: String   -- "if" | "unless" | "and" | "or" | "not"
-, value    :: Value    -- the evaluated condition value (so divergence is exact, not shape-approximated)
-, taken    :: Branch   -- then | else, under THIS engine's rule
-, diverges :: Array (Tuple String Branch)  -- named rules whose branch differs (see 3a)
-, path     :: Maybe Path   -- the data path, for bare-path conditions only (see 5)
-}
-----

-[[divergence]]*3a. Divergence is computed by replaying the named-rule lambdas* (Part A.2) against the
-recorded `value` — `handlebars`/`mustache-spec`/`minimal`/`presence`. The Mustache comparison rule is
-labelled `mustache-spec` (not plain `mustache`) precisely because `mustache.js` follows the
-`handlebars` rule, not the spec one: it never diverges from the engine here, so the report's legend says
-so and a `mustache.js` reader is not misled by a `mustache-spec` flip that does not apply to them (the S1
-clarification). No `FalsyShape` introspection is needed;
-this is *simpler* than the original set-replay design and depends only on the menu of built-in rules

-`diverges` is non-empty. Decisions on `false`/`null`/non-empty values are recorded too and surface as

-+
-[cols="1,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Value tested |Suggested fix in the report
-|`0` |`includeZero=true` (per-call); if 0 should stay falsy, `pass:[(ne x 0)]`
-|`pass:[""]` |make it explicit and rule-free: `pass:[(ne s "")]` / `pass:[(eq s "")]`
-|`pass:[[]]` |iterate — `pass:[{{#each xs}}…{{else}}…{{/each}}]` renders `else` on empty on every engine
-|`pass:[{}]` |only `presence` calls this falsy; test a known key explicitly

-The tag text shown per section is recovered by *slicing the template source at `span`* (the lexer already

-. *Surface: both the CLI and the Lab, sharing one `reportMarkdown`.* `flatbars analyse <template>

-  `?vendored=` corpus becomes a portability gallery). Both call the one

-  under a chosen rule was specced but **not built** — see the As-built note.) The learner-facing walkthrough

-
-. *JSONata cleanup is a reviewable scaffold, not a silent rewrite.* `--emit-jsonata` turns the *bare-path*

-  Bounded and stated in the output: computed-condition findings are listed but not emitted (no single
-  path), and "what *normalise* means" is a per-finding human choice, so the script is a scaffold the
-  author reviews — never applied automatically.
-
-== As-built (2026-06-05): where the implementation differs from this record
-
-Three deliberate simplifications landed differently from the decision text above;
-recorded here so the spec stops describing code that does not exist.
-
-* *The trace sink is a pure `WriterT`, not a `Ref` on `ExceptT Aff`.* Item 2 above
-  describes a closure-captured `Ref (Array Decision)` appended via `liftEffect`.
-  The implementation is `type AnalyseM = WriterT (Array Decision) (Either Error)`
-  — the wrappers `tell` a `Decision`; no `Effect`/`Ref`/`Aff`. This is *stricter
-  and simpler* than the spec (analysis is as pure as a normal render) and is the
-  shipped form.
-
-* *The `Decision` record is leaner.* The implemented record is
-  `{ span, op, value, truthyHere :: Boolean, diverges :: Array (Tuple String

-  carries the same information for the two-way control points) and no
-  `path :: Maybe Path` field. The data path (item 5) is recovered syntactically in
-  the *`Finding`* projection, not stored on `Decision`. Net behaviour is exactly as
-  specified; only the intermediate shape is smaller.
-
-* *`--rule` was not built.* The CLI ships `flatbars analyse <template> <data.json>
-  [--emit-jsonata]`; there is no `--rule` knob. The analysis always renders under
-  the engine's own rule and the report already lists *every* named rule that
-  flips, so a single-rule override added little. Deferred, not dropped — revisit
-  if a "show me only the Mustache delta" use case appears.
-
-The `presence` named rule remains (it is the rule under which `{}`/empty

-rather than branding it "ST4". The *StringTemplate4 source transpiler* that once

-the `st4` "ST4 Preview" output view, the `st4-modes` engine capability, the
-`transpileSt4`/`scanTruthinessPragma` machinery in `lab/playground_utils.mjs`, the
-`st4Mode` render-config option (with its `config.yaml` `st4_mode` field and the
-share-link `s4` flag), and the ST4 source highlighter are all gone, along with

-The Node-level gates (`npm run test:lab`) pass; the browser smoke (`lab/test`) is
-CI-only and still warrants a manual Lab boot to confirm the view strip and config

-
-== Consequences
-
-* *Net deletion, not addition.* Part A removes a 24-file configuration surface, a linter phase, and the
-  compiler's `$falsy` baking; Part B adds one observer module that reuses the engine. The hot render path
-  and the emitter get *simpler*.
-* *Drift-proof.* The named rules are the single source of truth for both rendering (Part A) and divergence
-  (Part B.3a); the analyser delegates to real operations, so it cannot disagree with a real render.
-* *The guarantee is data-relative, and the report says so.* "No findings" means *portable against this

-  corpus (a tracked follow-up — the data-driven harness).

-  "0 counts here" uses `includeZero` or an explicit `pass:[(ne x 0)]` — both portable, both surviving.
-
-== Alternatives considered
-
-* *Replace `FalsySet` with an opaque per-engine lambda (the original proposal).* Rejected as stated: an
-  opaque lambda is non-bakeable (breaks ADR-011) and makes Part B undecidable. Part A keeps the lambda

-* *Threading value provenance through `eval`.* Rejected: invasive for a benefit the syntactic tag-slice

-* *Docs cleanup.* xref:directives.adoc[] must drop the `@truthiness` directive/alias sections and re-cast

-= ADR-023: One recovering parser; fail-fast `parse` is its projection
-:navtitle: ADR-023 Recovering parser
-
-*Status:* Accepted; *implemented*. *Date:* 2026-06-03. Builds on
-xref:adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker.adoc[ADR-001] (one structural parser) and unblocks the
-editor diagnostics deferred by xref:adr-0017-editor-support-lsp.adoc[ADR-017].
-
-== Context
-
-ADR-017 shipped engine-backed *highlighting*, but left editor *diagnostics* (the red squiggle for a
-malformed tag) deferred behind a "recovering parser" it called a prerequisite. The naïve reading is that
-an IDE needs a second, error-tolerant parser alongside the engine's total, fail-fast `parse`. That is the
-exact *drift trap* this project fights everywhere else (ADR-001/014): two definitions of the grammar that
-must be kept in lock-step, and an IDE that can disagree with the compiler about what is even valid.
-
-The core also distinguishes a *fail-fast* contract the compiler genuinely needs — you cannot codegen a
-syntactically invalid template, so `parse` must be total and reject bad input — from the *implementation*
-that delivers it. The question is whether fail-fast must be dropped, kept as a second engine, or
-re-expressed.
-
-A template language makes recovery unusually tractable: the lexer (`tokenizeTemplate`) already delimits
-tags into a flat `RawTok` stream, so *tag boundaries are natural synchronization points*. An error in one
-tag's interior need not blank the rest of the document.
-
-== Decision
-
-. *There is ONE parser, and it recovers.* `parseSeq` (the tree builder over the `RawTok` stream) no
-  longer returns `Either`: it always produces a best-effort tree plus *every* error in source order. The
-  recovery is local and bounded, anchored at tag boundaries:
-+
---
-* a tag with a bad interior drops a `NodeError Span String` marker and the scan continues;
-* a *block* opener with a salvageable head (a leading identifier — `pass:[{{#if a == 1}}]` yields name
-  `if` even though the args won't parse) still nests, so its body and close parse and only the bad args
-  are flagged — no cascade of spurious errors;
-* a missing or mismatched `pass:[{{/x}}]` builds the block anyway and records the mismatch; a stray
-  top-level close is reported and recovered past.
---
-
-. *Fail-fast is kept, but re-expressed as a PROJECTION over the recovering parser — not dropped, not a
-  second engine.* `parse` / `parseWith` run `parseRecovering` and return `Right tree` iff no error was
-  recovered, else `Left` the first error in source order — byte-for-byte the result the total parser
-  always gave. The compiler/render path keeps its total, fail-fast contract; it simply gets the verdict
-  from the one parser. Editor tooling calls `parseRecovering` directly. *One grammar, two views — drift
-  is impossible by construction*, which is ADR-001's principle, now fulfilled more truly (a fail-fast-only
-  parser is exactly what would have forced a second one).
-+
-The cost on a *valid* template is zero: recovery only triggers on an error, and on the error path the
-compiler rejects the file anyway, so the extra work is never wasted on output.
-
-. *`NodeError` is a first-class AST node.* It carries the offending span and a message and appears *only*
-  in a `parseRecovering` tree. Because `parse` projects any recovered error to `Left`, the render /
-  compile / lower / desugar paths never receive one; each consumer's `NodeError` arm is a total,
-  unreachable-in-practice neutral (the foldTemplate algebra gained a `nodeError` case). Tooling folds
-  (diagnostics, pretty-print) handle it meaningfully. We chose an in-tree node over a sidecar error list
-  so a later phase (hover, selection ranges) can attach to the error's position in the tree.
-
-. *Diagnostics are derived, not heuristic.* `flatbars-js` exposes `diagnostics(template, dialect)` —
-  `parseRecovering` with that dialect's `ParseOptions`, each error located via `parseErrorAt`. The same
-  dialect seam that makes `==` an operator in MaxBars makes `pass:[{{#if a == 1}}]` an error in every
-  other surface — so the editor flags exactly what the dialect rejects. `flatbars-lsp` publishes these as
-  `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` on open and every edit.
-
-== Consequences
-
-* Editor diagnostics work, four dialects, with no second parser and no change to the fail-fast contract.
-  ADR-017's "recovering parser (prerequisite)" open question is resolved by this record.
-* `parse`/`parseWith` stay byte-compatible — every spago suite passes and `test:compile` is 296/296
-  (compiled ≡ interpreter). The recovering behaviour has its own tests (`parseRecovering`).
-* `NodeError` widens the `Node` sum, so every match on it is total by construction; a new consumer of the
-  skeleton AST must add a `nodeError` arm (a one-line neutral unless it is tooling).
-* *Deferred, not blocked:* richer recovery for an unsalvageable block head (currently a `NodeError` plus a
-  flat tail), and hover/completion built on the in-tree error nodes. Diagnostic *ranges* currently cover
-  the offending tag (start → its `}}`); finer spans can come from `NodeError`'s span when needed.
-
-== Amendment (2026-06-04): recovery over pre-lexed interiors
-
-`headedRecovering`/`salvageName` now consume each tag's *pre-lexed* interior,
-carried on the `RawTok` itself and populated by `tokenizeTemplate`
-(xref:adr-0004-token-lexer-and-grammar-seams.adoc[ADR-004] amendment), instead of
-re-lexing it. Per-tag recovery is preserved precisely because that interior is the
-*deferred* `Either ParseError (Array PosToken)`: a malformed interior is a `Left`
-that rides inside its own tag and is handled exactly where `tokenizeInterior` used
-to fail, so one bad tag never breaks the structural scan or the rest of the
-document. Behaviour is unchanged (`parseRecovering` tests + `test:compile` 300/300).

-:navtitle: ADR-024 `let` & dict literal
-
-*Status:* Proposed (revised 2026-06-04 after team review — see *Resolved during review* below; the list
-literal was split out to xref:adr-0025-list-literal.adoc[ADR-025]).
-*Date:* 2026-06-04. Applies to *MaxBars and RawBars* only; *FullBars is unchanged*
-(Handlebars-faithful — see xref:adr-0009-fullbars.adoc[ADR-009] and the conformance line at
-xref:adr-0005-dialect-ladder.adoc[ADR-005]). Sits alongside
-xref:adr-0021-maxbars-variable-model.adoc[ADR-021] (the MaxBars/RawBars variable model) as the
-expression-sugar half of the same dialect carve-out.
-
-This ADR covers the two constructs that need *no shared-prelude change*: block-scoped `{{#let}}` and the
-dict literal (which reuses the existing `dict` helper). The *list literal* needs a new `list` constructor
-in the shared prelude, a different blast radius, so it is its own decision —
-xref:adr-0025-list-literal.adoc[ADR-025]. The two ADRs share this Context and the lexing/dialect model.
-
-== Context
-
-Template authors recurringly need *template-local constants* — a forge-name → URL lookup table, a
-status → label enum, an alias for a deep path used many times — that are intrinsic to the template,
-identical on every render, and have no business in the host data. Today the only spelling is to pass
-them in through the render context on every call, which is friction for what is effectively a `const`
-inside the template.
-
-Three things make this a design problem, not a one-helper fix:
-
-* *No variables.* The xref:concepts.adoc[concepts] thesis is strict — *"the only compound expression is
-  an application of a name."* Any new construct must either *be* an application or *desugar* to one. A
-  literal expression class (`Lit`-typed nodes for `{…}`/`[…]`) cannot live in the kernel AST.
-* *No host-format dependency in core.* xref:adr-0003-strict-layering.adoc[ADR-003] keeps `JSON` ⇆ `Value`
-  out of the core (*"JSON-ness is a host concern"*). YAML / JSON-style literal collections in *tag*
-  bodies would re-import the same dependency under a different name.
-* *Dialect carve-out is the established lever.* xref:adr-0005-dialect-ladder.adoc[ADR-005] gives MaxBars
-  the room for surface additions FullBars cannot have, by reuse-by-dependency: MaxBars depends on
-  `fullbars`, swaps the interior expression grammar, and FullBars's Handlebars conformance
-  (`49/50` byte-identical, gated by `check:hbs-conformance`) is untouched. xref:adr-0006-maxbars-loop-variables.adoc[ADR-006]
-  /xref:adr-0021-maxbars-variable-model.adoc[ADR-021] use this for the variable model; this ADR uses it
-  for `let` and the dict literal.
-
-The space of candidates was enumerated in the design debate. The salient negative results — captured
-here so future revivals don't relitigate, and shared with xref:adr-0025-list-literal.adoc[ADR-025] —
-were:
-
-* *JSON-style literals* (`{"b":1,"c":2}`, `[1,2,3]`) — imported `:` and `,` as new tag-body tokens with
-  no FlatBars precedent, broke whitespace-separated args, doubled the editor-tooling contract
-  (xref:adr-0017-editor-support-lsp.adoc[ADR-017] token-vocabulary).
-* *Unified `[…]` for both dicts and lists*, content-disambiguated (all-`name=value` ⇒ dict, otherwise
-  list). Killed by the empty-collection case: `[]` cannot mean both, leaving no literal spelling for
-  the empty dict — and discarded the universal `{} / []` shape convention every comparable language
-  (including Lua's tables) honours. This is *why* the dict literal is `{…}` (here) and the list literal
-  is `[…]` (ADR-025), as two distinct shapes.
-* *Dict sugar at the helper level only* (e.g. renaming `dict` → `obj`). One character saved per call,
-  capped by name quality; not worth a prelude churn on a well-established helper.
-* *Dropping `{{#with}}` in favour of `{{#let}}`*. `with` does two jobs (re-root context + optional alias);
-  `let` does one (alias only). The aliases are equivalent only when the body never uses bare names. `with`
-  also lives in the shared prelude, so removing it requires either splitting the prelude or adding a
-  surface-level rejection — both heavier than the saving. See *Relationship to `{{#with}}`* below.
-
-== Decision
-
-Two constructs ship here, scoped to *MaxBars only*, *surface-stage* desugared, with *no shared-prelude
-change*: block-scoped `{{#let}}` and the dict literal. (The list literal and its required `list` helper
-are xref:adr-0025-list-literal.adoc[ADR-025].)
-
-=== 1. Block-scoped `{{#let}}` — alias only, never re-root
-
-`{{#let}}` installs *nullary operations* at the block's lexical scope; they vanish at `{{/let}}`. It is
-the operation model applied to template-local *constants* — no new concept, just a new way to write one.
-
-[source,handlebars]
-----
-{{#let n=expr [n=expr …]}}
-  … body where each n is a nullary operation that returns expr …
-{{/let}}
-----
-
-Semantics:
-
-* *Bindings* evaluate left-to-right, each in the scope *extended by the bindings to its left*: in
-  `pass:[{{#let a=1 b=(add a 1)}}]`, `b` sees `a`. A binding sees neither itself nor any binding to its
-  right, so there is no self-reference and no fixpoint — this is a *sequential* `let`, not a `letrec`,
-  and it remains a single total walk (no second pass). The sequential form removes the nesting tax the
-  earlier parallel design imposed (which forced `pass:[{{#let a=1}}{{#let b=(add a 1)}} … {{/let}}{{/let}}]`
-  for what is the common case).
-* *Scope* is block-scoped lexically: names exist between `{{#let}}` and `{{/let}}`. Inner blocks inherit;
-  partials called inside inherit (the standing scope-chain rule).
-* *Shadowing.* A `let` name that collides with an in-scope helper shadows it inside the body, then the
-  original is unshadowed at `{{/let}}`. A collision with a `{{#each xs as |x|}}` block param of the same
-  name in the *same* scope is a parse error.
-* *Does not re-root context.* `{{#let u=user}}{{name}}{{/let}}` resolves `name` against the *root*, not
-  against `user`. To re-root, use `{{#with}}` (which stays — see below).
-
-=== 2. Dict literal `{name=expr name=expr …}` — MaxBars expression sugar
-
-A brace-delimited list of hash-arg pairs in expression position is sugar for `(dict …)`. The interior
-syntax is FlatBars-native — *bare* keys, `=` separator, *whitespace*-separated pairs — no JSON
-conventions are imported.
-
-[source,handlebars]
-----
-{{#let forges={codeberg="…" github="…" gitlab="…"}}}
-  …
-{{/let}}
-----
-
-Desugars at the MaxBars parser stage to `pass:[(dict codeberg="…" github="…" gitlab="…")]`. The `dict`
-helper already lives in the shared prelude (xref:prelude.adoc[]); *no kernel or prelude change* — this is
-the property that lets the dict literal ship ahead of the list literal.
-
-Empty: `{}` is the empty dict — clean, unambiguous, lowers to `(dict)`.
-
-=== 3. Lexing: desugar at the MaxBars expression stage, structure lexer untouched
-
-The dict literal is resolved entirely in the MaxBars interior grammar (`MaxBars.Expr`, plugged in
-through the `ParseOptions.parseExpr` seam). The *structure* lexer (`tokenizeTemplate`) never gains `{` or
-`}` as structural tokens, and tag-boundary detection is unchanged. This is what keeps the three
-delimiter widths (`{{ }}` / `{{{ }}}` / `{{{{ }}}}`) intact: width detection runs *first* and fixes the
-tag span; only then does the interior tokenizer see the literal braces. (ADR-025 extends the same
-principle to `[`/`]`; the rule is identical.)
-
-The one consequence for the surface: inside an already-delimited tag, the interior tokenizer matches `{`
-against its closing `}` by nesting depth, so a literal collection's own closing brace is consumed before
-the tag close. `pass:[{{#let x={a=1}}}]` therefore reads as `#let x=` · `{a=1}` · `}}` (dict-close, then
-tag-close), and the nested `pass:[{{#let x={a={b=1}}}}}]` as `{a={b=1}}` · `}}` — no ambiguity, because
-the tag span was settled by width detection before the interior is scanned. *Authors never insert a
-disambiguating space.* This is the load-bearing lexing claim, so it is gated by a dedicated tokenizer
-corpus (see *Gates*).
-
-=== 4. Dialect scope
-
-[cols="1,1,1,1",options="header"]
-|===
-| Surface | `{{#let}}` | `{…}` dict literal | Notes
-| *RawBars* | ✓ (explicit form: `pass:[{{#let (bind a x)}}…{{/let}}]`) | ✗ (no sugar at all by design) | Writes the kernel form directly.
-| *FullBars* | *✗* | *✗* | Handlebars-faithful. Authors use `pass:[{{#with x as \|n\|}}]` for aliasing and `(dict …)` for collections.
-| *MaxBars* | ✓ (with `n=expr` surface sugar) | ✓ (`{name=expr …}`) | The flagship; the list literal is added by ADR-025.
-|===
-
-This is the same asymmetry already enforced for MaxBars operators (`>=` is MaxBars-only sugar that
-lowers to `(gte …)`; `gte` is a shared-prelude helper).
-
-=== 5. Kernel footprint
-
-One addition, small and decided here (not deferred):
-
-* *A dedicated `Let [(name, expr)] body` AST node* (resolved during review — see below). It pushes a
-  helpers-only frame onto the env stack at `{{#let}}` and pops it at `{{/let}}`. The env stack already
-  exists — `pushFrame` (`Kernel.Env`) is what block params and `{{#with}}` use — but note `pushFrame`
-  bundles *helpers + context*; `let` pushes the binding helpers while *passing the current context
-  through unchanged* (that is the "never re-root" guarantee of §1, expressed mechanically). No new
-  `Value` shape.
-
-The dict literal adds *nothing* to the kernel: `{…}` desugars before the AST is built, so the kernel sees
-an ordinary `Application` node — `(dict …)` — and `dict` is already in the prelude. (The list literal of
-ADR-025 is the one construct that *does* touch the shared prelude.)
-
-=== 6. Relationship to `{{#with}}`
-
-`{{#with}}` stays in *every* dialect. `let` and `with` are complements, not competitors:
-
-[cols="2,1,1",options="header"]
-|===
-| Operation | Alias | Re-root `this` / bare names
-| `pass:[{{#let n=x}}]` | ✓ | ✗
-| `pass:[{{#with x}}]` | ✗ | ✓
-| `pass:[{{#with x as \|n\|}}]` | ✓ | ✓
-|===
-
-The identity worth recording: `pass:[{{#with x as |n|}}]` ≡ `pass:[{{#with x}}{{#let n=x}} … {{/let}}{{/with}}]`.
-`let` desugars *part* of `with`, not the whole thing.
-
-== Consequences
-
-=== Gates
-
-* *Tokenizer corpus (precondition — must land before implementation).* A golden corpus in the
-  `check:highlight` style that pins the lexing claim of §3 over the adjacent-brace cases: `pass:[{{#let x={a=1}}}]`,
-  `pass:[{{#let x={}}}]`, and the nested `pass:[{{#let x={a={b=1}}}}}]` (five trailing braces). Each must
-  tokenize with the tag span fixed by width detection *before* the interior is scanned. No corpus, no
-  merge — this is the construct's highest-risk surface. (ADR-025 adds the bracket cases.)
-* *`check:hbs-conformance`* — already in `npm test`. Catches any FullBars regression from the `49/50`
-  byte-identical line. If `let`/`{…}` ever bleed into the FullBars surface parser, the next run of this
-  gate flags it. (Unlike ADR-025, this ADR adds no prelude helper, so there is no catalog/conformance
-  churn here.)
-* *`check:isolation`* — extended with one MaxBars-only-surface assertion per construct, source-pinned in
-  the style of `check:a11y`: a FullBars template containing `pass:[{{#let …}}]` or `{name=expr}` in
-  expression position must produce a surface diagnostic, not silent acceptance.
-* *Linter round-trip* (`Linter.Lower`) — pins that `pass:[{{#let a=1}}]` lowers to
-  `pass:[{{#let (bind a 1)}}]` and `{b=1 c=2}` lowers to `pass:[(dict b=1 c=2)]`. One canonical RawBars
-  form per construct — no AST drift, no two-way sugar.
-
-=== Linter
-
-* New hint *`prefer-let-over-with-as`* (MaxBars only): suggest `pass:[{{#let n=x}}…{{/let}}]` when the
-  body of a `pass:[{{#with x as |n|}}…{{/with}}]` never uses bare names — the exact case where the
-  forms are equivalent. *Soundness boundary:* the scope-chain rule (§1) means a partial invoked in the
-  body inherits the re-rooted context and may consume bare names *invisibly* — and a host-supplied
-  partial cannot be analysed at all. So the hint fires *only when the body invokes no partial*
-  (`pass:[{{> …}}]`, `pass:[{{#> …}}]`, `pass:[{{yield}}]`); a body that calls a partial is left alone
-  rather than risk a rewrite that changes rendering. The genuine `with` use-cases (re-root with no
-  alias, or re-root + alias with a bare-name body) are untouched.
-
-=== Editor tooling (ADR-017 contract)
-
-The token vocabulary gains two new tag-body tokens, scoped to the MaxBars grammar variant: `{` and `}`
-(the dict literal's delimiters). The LSP semantic-token emitter, the TextMate fallback grammar, and the
-VS Code / JetBrains extension grammars each receive a one-time update; the *contract source*
-(xref:adr-0017-editor-support-lsp.adoc[ADR-017] token-vocabulary.json) is the single edit point. (ADR-025
-adds the `[`/`]` tokens, including the `[` dual-context disambiguation.)
-
-=== Documentation
-
-* `maxbars.adoc` gains a `Let` section and a `Dict literal` section.
-* `rawbars.adoc` adds one paragraph: the explicit `pass:[(bind …)]` form is the desugared canonical;
-  surface sugar lives in MaxBars.
-* `fullbars.adoc` is *not* modified. The existing convention rule in `tutorials/src/fullbars.mjs`
-  (*"No MaxBars operators"*) gains a parallel line: *"No MaxBars block-scoped bindings, no MaxBars dict
-  literals."*
-
-=== Non-goals (deliberately deferred)
-
-* *File-level front matter* (template-scoped data via a `---` YAML header). A host-layer concern (see
-  the front-matter debate notes); `let` is the engine-side, lexically-scoped answer. If a front-matter
-  adapter ships later it should *desugar at the host* into a top-level `let` — keeping one canonical
-  binding mechanism.
-* *Dropping `{{#with}}`* in MaxBars/RawBars. Considered and rejected — the carve-out cost exceeds the
-  gain, and the philosophical objection (`with` re-roots ⇒ "hidden variable") already coexists with
-  `{{#each}}`'s identical re-rooting. The linter hint covers the cases where `let` would actually
-  read more clearly.
-
-== Resolved during review
-
-The team review of 2026-06-04 closed the questions that were previously left open or mis-scoped:
-
-* *The list literal was split out to xref:adr-0025-list-literal.adoc[ADR-025].* It alone needs a new
-  `list` constructor in the *shared* prelude (the prelude has no list constructor today), so it carries a
-  catalog + conformance blast radius that `let` and the dict literal do not. Keeping them in one ADR
-  conflated "pure MaxBars surface" with "shared-prelude change"; the split makes each decision honest and
-  lets `let` + dict ship first.
-* *Kernel primitive: a dedicated `Let [(name, expr)] body` AST node*, not a sugar that lowers to a chain
-  of single-binding scope-frame ops. The runtime behaviour is identical, but the `Linter.Lower`
-  round-trip is a *stated gate* (see *Consequences*), and it cannot be specified without fixing the
-  canonical form: a dedicated node round-trips one-to-one, whereas the sugar-chain lowers
-  `pass:[{{#let a=1 b=2}}]` to *nested* `(bind)` blocks — two-way drift, the exact failure the gate
-  exists to prevent. So the node is the canonical form.
-* *Binding semantics are sequential* (§1), not parallel-in-the-enclosing-scope. The dedicated node makes
-  forward reference (`b` sees `a`) free, and it matches every author's mental model of `let` while
-  staying a single total walk.

-= ADR-025: The list literal `[…]` and the `list` prelude helper — MaxBars surface + shared prelude
-:navtitle: ADR-025 list literal
-
-*Status:* Proposed. *Date:* 2026-06-04. The list-literal half of the collection-literal design,
-*split from* xref:adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal.adoc[ADR-024] during the 2026-06-04 team review.
-Applies to *MaxBars* (surface sugar) and the *shared prelude* (a new constructor). FullBars's surface is
-*unchanged*; the prelude addition is value-only and Handlebars-compatible (gated by
-`check:hbs-conformance`).
-
-This is a separate ADR from xref:adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal.adoc[ADR-024] for one reason: the
-list literal is *not* pure MaxBars surface. Its desugar target does not exist, so it ships a new helper
-into the *shared* prelude — a different blast radius (catalog regen, conformance re-run, presence in
-every dialect) than `let` and the dict literal, both of which reuse what is already there. Conflating the
-two understated this cost; separating them keeps each decision honest and lets ADR-024 ship first.
-
-== Context
-
-Shared with the *Context* of xref:adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal.adoc[ADR-024] — the
-template-local-constants motivation, the *no variables* / *no host-format-in-core* constraints, the
-dialect carve-out lever, and the enumerated negative results (JSON-style literals; the unified-`[…]`
-dead-end that forces distinct `{…}`/`[…]` shapes). Not repeated here.
-
-One fact specific to lists drives this ADR:
-
-* *There is no list constructor today.* The shared prelude (xref:prelude.adoc[]) has list-_consuming_
-  helpers — `join`, `count`, `size`, `at`, `take`, `reverse`, `unique`, `pluck` — but nothing that
-  *builds* a list. The only way to obtain one is `split` (from a string). So a template author cannot
-  write a literal sequence at all. This is a genuine capability gap, not a convenience over an existing
-  helper (contrast `dict`, which `(dict …)` has always provided). The list literal closes it, and that
-  is why it is worth a prelude addition.
-
-== Decision
-
-Two things ship together, because the surface sugar is inert without its target:
-
-=== 1. A new `list` prelude helper
-
-A variadic value helper `pass:[(list e …)]` that returns the array of its evaluated arguments. It lives
-in the *shared* prelude next to `dict`, so it is available in every dialect's expression position
-(RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars/MinBars), exactly as `dict` is. It adds no new `Value` shape (arrays already
-exist) and no kernel change — it is an ordinary value-producing operation, the list analogue of `dict`.
-
-This is the one piece that distinguishes this ADR from xref:adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal.adoc[ADR-024]:
-a *shared-prelude* change, with the catalog + conformance consequences in *Gates* below.
-
-=== 2. List literal `[expr expr …]` — MaxBars expression sugar
-
-A bracket-delimited list of positional expressions in expression position is sugar for `(list …)`.
-
-[source,handlebars]
-----
-{{#let langs=["PureScript" "TypeScript" "Rust"]}}
-  {{#each langs}} — {{this}}{{/each}}
-{{/let}}
-----
-
-Desugars at the MaxBars parser stage to `pass:[(list "PureScript" "TypeScript" "Rust")]`. Empty: `[]` is
-the empty list, lowers to `(list)`. The sugar is MaxBars-only; RawBars writes `(list …)` directly;
-FullBars has neither the sugar nor (by convention) uses it, though the `list` helper is *present* in its
-prelude.
-
-=== 3. Lexing and the `[` / `.[` disambiguation
-
-Lexing follows the *Lexing* section of xref:adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal.adoc[ADR-024]
-verbatim, extended from `{`/`}` to `[`/`]`: desugar happens in the MaxBars interior grammar
-(`MaxBars.Expr` via the `ParseOptions.parseExpr` seam); the *structure* lexer never gains `[`/`]` as
-structural tokens; width detection fixes the tag span before the interior is scanned, so a literal's own
-`]` is consumed by nesting depth before the tag close. `pass:[{{#let xs=[1 2]}}}]`… reads cleanly, and no
-disambiguating space is ever required.
-
-The one list-specific hazard is the existing path-index form `pass:[{{a.[i]}}]`. The disambiguation is
-*not* by look-behind — that is unsound under the recovering parser
-(xref:adr-0023-recovering-parser.adoc[ADR-023]), where the preceding token may be a `NodeError`. Instead,
-in the MaxBars interior grammar *`.[` is the only path-index form*; a `[` in any other position is
-unconditionally a list-open. The two productions never compete for the same token, so error recovery on a
-malformed tag cannot flip one into the other. (This is the one claim flagged for a confirming tokenizer
-spike — see *Open question*.)
-
-=== 4. Dialect scope
-
-[cols="1,1,1",options="header"]
-|===
-| Surface | `[…]` list literal | `(list …)` helper
-| *RawBars* | ✗ (no sugar by design) | ✓ (write it directly)
-| *FullBars* | ✗ (Handlebars-faithful surface) | ✓ (present in the shared prelude; convention says don't use it)
-| *MaxBars* | ✓ (`[expr …]`) | ✓
-|===
-
-The helper is shared (a value-policy-free constructor, like `dict`); only the *sugar* is MaxBars-scoped —
-the same asymmetry as `>=` → `(gte …)`.
-
-== Consequences
-
-=== Gates
-
-* *`check:catalog`* — the new `list` helper makes the generated helper catalog stale; run
-  `npm run gen:catalog` and the gate keeps the docs partial in step with `FullBars.preludeSchema`. *This
-  gate is the headline difference from xref:adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal.adoc[ADR-024]*, which
-  adds no helper.
-* *`check:hbs-conformance`* — already in `npm test`. Re-run after adding `list` to confirm the `49/50`
-  byte-identical FullBars line is unmoved (a value-producing helper should be inert to it, but the gate
-  proves it). Also catches any `[…]` bleed into the FullBars surface parser.
-* *Tokenizer corpus (precondition — must land before implementation).* Extends the ADR-024 corpus with
-  the bracket cases: `pass:[{{#let xs=[]}}]`, `pass:[{{#let xs=[1 2 3]}}]`, the mixed
-  `pass:[{{#let x={a=[1 2]}}}}]` (four trailing braces), and the path-index control `pass:[{{a.[0]}}]` to
-  pin that `.[` is *not* read as a list-open. No corpus, no merge.
-* *`check:isolation`* — one MaxBars-only-surface assertion: a FullBars template with `[expr …]` in
-  expression position produces a surface diagnostic, not silent acceptance. (Note the `list` *helper* is
-  legal everywhere; only the bracket *sugar* is gated.)
-* *Linter round-trip* (`Linter.Lower`) — pins that `[1 2 3]` lowers to `pass:[(list 1 2 3)]`. One
-  canonical RawBars form, no two-way sugar.
-
-=== Editor tooling (ADR-017 contract)
-
-The token vocabulary gains two new tag-body tokens, scoped to the MaxBars grammar variant: `[` and `]`.
-The `[` token has two lexical contexts within tags — path-index in `.[` (existing) and list-literal
-elsewhere (new); §3 fixes the disambiguation to be position-based, not look-behind-based, so it is robust
-under the recovering parser. The LSP semantic-token emitter, the TextMate fallback grammar, and the VS
-Code / JetBrains grammars each receive a one-time update; the contract source
-(xref:adr-0017-editor-support-lsp.adoc[ADR-017] token-vocabulary.json) is the single edit point.
-
-=== Documentation
-
-* `maxbars.adoc` gains a `List literal` subsection (alongside the `Dict literal` section added by
-  xref:adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal.adoc[ADR-024]).
-* `prelude.adoc` / the generated helper catalog gain the `list` entry (via `gen:catalog`).
-* `rawbars.adoc` notes `(list …)` as the canonical form behind the MaxBars `[…]` sugar.
-* `fullbars.adoc` convention line (`tutorials/src/fullbars.mjs`) extends to *"no MaxBars list literals"*
-  (the `list` helper itself stays available, like any prelude value helper).
-
-=== Non-goals (deliberately deferred)
-
-* *Bracket literals outside `{{#let}}`*. A natural future extension is `pass:[{{#each [1 2 3]}}…{{/each}}]`
-  and `pass:[(map [1 2 3] …)]` — admissible because, once this ADR lands, `pass:[(list …)]` is a
-  first-class expression. Out of scope here; opens cleanly if pressure shows up.
-* *A `map`/`filter`/`fold` family over lists.* The list literal makes such helpers *useful*, but each is
-  its own prelude decision; this ADR ships only the constructor.
-
-== Open question
-
-The §3 claim that *`.[` is the only path-index form and every other `[` is a list-open* is the one piece
-not yet proven against the recovering parser. Before the four editor grammars
-(xref:adr-0017-editor-support-lsp.adoc[ADR-017]) are touched, a small tokenizer spike should confirm that
-malformed-tag recovery never reclassifies a path-index `[` as a list-open (and vice versa). The
-implementation is otherwise straightforward; this is the only residual risk, and it is contained to the
-MaxBars interior tokenizer.

-= ADR-026 — Editor capability matrix
-:adr-id: 0026
-:status: Accepted
-:date: 2026-06-04
-
-== Context
-
-ADR-017 set the two-layer model — TextMate grammar (the floor) plus
-`flatbars-lsp` semantic tokens (the ceiling) — and shipped the minimum LSP
-surface needed to demonstrate it: `semanticTokens/full`, `publishDiagnostics`,
-`textDocument/hover`, `textDocument/completion`, and a `codeAction`
-canonicalisation quick-fix.
-
-The June 2026 editor-plugin review surfaced a follow-up question: what is the
-*complete* set of LSP capabilities the editors advertise, and which IDE-native
-features (Find Usages, Rename, Reformat, Structure View, Folding, Breadcrumbs,
-Go to Definition) is the plugin expected to provide? The platform LSP client in
-JetBrains does not auto-wire most of those; the server must both advertise the
-capability and the editor side must opt in.
-
-This ADR fixes the matrix.
-
-== Decision
-
-The editors ship the following LSP capabilities, gated on what the engine can
-honestly compute from a *single* template document (the FlatBars engine does
-not maintain a cross-template scope graph, by design — partials are looked up
-by name in a host-supplied registry, see ADR-003):
-
-|===
-| Capability | Status | Source
-
-| `semanticTokens/full`
-| Ship
-| ADR-017 — engine `tokenize` + vocab-driven legend. The legend is augmented
-  with one *custom* semantic-token type — `embeddedDelimiter` — declared in
-  `editors/token-vocabulary.json` under `customSemanticTypes` and codegenned
-  into the VS Code manifest's `contributes.semanticTokenTypes` +
-  `semanticTokenScopes` so the LSP-emitted brace pair under a switched
-  delimiter (`{{=<% %>=}}` → subsequent `<% … %>`) themes identically to the
-  grammar's `punctuation.section.embedded.flatbars` floor without per-theme
-  work. `check:vocab` enforces parity between the kind's `lsp.type` and the
-  custom-type declaration.
-
-| `publishDiagnostics`
-| Ship
-| ADR-023 — recovering parser → `NodeError` ranges. The LSP layers a second
-  diagnostic source on top — `dialectDiagnostics` in `editors/lsp/src/tokens.mjs`
-  — a small finder array that flags surface constructs the *engine* accepts
-  but the *dialect* does not (e.g. set-delim outside MinBars, MaxBars `??` in
-  any other dialect, subexpressions / block params / partial-hash-args / helper
-  invocations in MinBars). Each finder produces an actionable, dialect-named
-  message instead of leaving the user with an opaque parse failure. The rule
-  inventory is pinned by `check:dialect-diagnostics` so refactoring the finders
-  array cannot silently drop a rule.
-
-| `textDocument/hover`
-| Ship
-| `operations.json` derived from `FullBars.preludeSchema`.
-
-| `textDocument/completion`
-| Ship
-| Same source as hover, gated on `inTagContext`.
-
-| `textDocument/codeAction`
-| Ship
-| Canonicalisation rewrites (`index` → `index0`, `partial-block` → `yield`).
-
-| `textDocument/foldingRange`
-| Ship (new)
-| Every block-open / block-close pair is a fold region; raw-block regions fold.
-  Single-document, structurally trivial from the engine tokens.
-
-| `textDocument/documentSymbol`
-| Ship (new)
-| The block nesting hierarchy projected as a symbol tree — feeds IntelliJ
-  Structure View and VS Code outline.
-
-| `textDocument/formatting`
-| Ship (new)
-| Canonical-spacing inside `{{ … }}` (one space after the opener, one before
-  the closer, normalised internal whitespace). Single-document, deterministic.
-
-| Bold tag emphasis ("isle in the ocean")
-| Ship (new)
-| The whole tag — braces + interior — renders bold. VS Code: vocab-driven
-  `configurationDefaults` (overridable), bold on every theme + injected hosts.
-  JetBrains: bold on the LSP ceiling only (`lspCustomization` semantic-token
-  attributes); the TextMate floor stays theme-controlled (no plugin hook to
-  force a scope's font weight) — the same Ultimate-vs-Community asymmetry as LSP.
-
-| `textDocument/definition`
-| Do not ship
-| Would require a cross-template scope graph (which partial defines which
-  identifier, where a `{{> partial}}` resolves). FlatBars uses a runtime
-  partial registry the engine never indexes; building an editor-time index
-  duplicates the host's data and would drift. Out of scope for the editor.
-
-| `textDocument/references`
-| Do not ship
-| Same reason as definition: no global identifier graph.
-
-| `textDocument/rename`
-| Do not ship
-| Same reason; refactoring partial names would have to coordinate with the
-  host application's partial registry.
-

-= ADR-027 — Cross-template scope graph for the LSP
-:adr-id: 0027
-:status: Proposed
-:date: 2026-06-04
-
-== Context
-
-xref:adr-0026-editor-capability-matrix.adoc[ADR-026] fixed the LSP capability
-matrix and listed four capabilities the server deliberately does NOT ship —
-`textDocument/definition`, `textDocument/references`, `textDocument/rename`,
-`textDocument/documentHighlight` — on the grounds that the engine has no
-cross-template scope graph: partials and helpers are looked up at runtime
-through a host-supplied registry the engine never indexes. Without an editor-
-side index, those four capabilities would either return nothing or fall back
-to text-shaped string search (strictly worse than the editor's built-in word
-highlight).
-
-This record proposes the missing scope graph as a *separate, future work
-item* outside the editor surface — an engine-level addition that, once
-shipped, would unlock the four LSP capabilities almost mechanically.
-
-== Decision
-
-A cross-template scope graph is a workspace-scoped index built and maintained
-by the language server, structured around the two named references FlatBars
-templates actually carry:
-
-* **Partial names** — every `{{> name}}` (and `{{#> name}}`) is a reference;
-  every `{{#*inline "name"}} … {{/inline}}` block (FullBars) is a definition.
-* **Helper / operation names** — every identifier the painter resolves
-  through `editors/operations.json` is a reference to the catalogue entry;
-  user-defined helpers registered via `registerHelper` (ADR-018) are
-  definitions only the host knows about (out of editor scope until the
-  registry abstraction lands).
-
-The index is workspace-rooted: the LSP scans every file whose URI extension
-maps to a dialect (`dialectForUri` returns non-null), parses each into the
-token stream, and records `(name, defLocation)` and `(name, refLocation)`
-tuples. Two collections per workspace:
-
-* `partialDefinitions: Map<name, Location[]>` — the locations of inline
-  declarations.
-* `partialReferences: Map<name, Location[]>` — the locations of `{{> name}}`
-  invocations.
-
-Capability wiring:
-
-* `textDocument/definition` on a partial-name token (in either an inline
-  declaration or an invocation) returns the matching definitions.
-* `textDocument/references` returns all matching invocations (plus the
-  definition when `includeDeclaration` is set).
-* `textDocument/rename` proposes a `WorkspaceEdit` rewriting both the
-  definition and every invocation.
-* `textDocument/documentHighlight` (the in-file slice) returns the
-  definitions and references that share the file with the cursor.
-
-The index is *eventually consistent*: built on `workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles`,
-re-indexed per-file on `textDocument/didChange`, garbage-collected on
-`textDocument/didClose` when the URI leaves the workspace. The LSP serves
-stale answers between batches rather than blocking on a full re-scan — the
-worst stale answer is "no result" which the four capabilities tolerate.
-

-
-. **Phase 1 — read-only scanner.** Add `editors/lsp/src/index.mjs` that
-  consumes the engine's `tokenize` over every workspace file and builds the
-  two maps. No LSP wiring yet; expose `definitionsOf(name)` /
-  `referencesOf(name)` for tests.
-. **Phase 2 — `textDocument/definition` + `documentHighlight`.** Wire the
-  first two capabilities into `server.mjs`; advertise both in the
-  `InitializeResult`. The single-buffer documentHighlight degrades to the
-  word-bounded set of references in the active file when the index is cold.
-. **Phase 3 — `textDocument/references`.** Same shape as definition; honours
-  `includeDeclaration`.
-. **Phase 4 — `textDocument/rename`.** Returns a `WorkspaceEdit` with one
-  `TextEdit` per occurrence. A pre-check rejects renames whose target collides
-  with an existing partial name.
-. **Phase 5 — helper / operation references.** Treat catalogue identifiers as
-  references too; the catalogue entries themselves are the definitions
-  (synthetic locations into `operations.json`).
-
-Tests at each phase: per-fixture corpus under `editors/lsp/test/fixtures/`
-asserting the index's contents, the capability's response, and at least one
-multi-file scenario.
-
-== Consequences
-
-* Unblocks the four ADR-026 omissions without requiring a language-level
-  module system. The engine itself stays unchanged — the LSP owns the index.
-* Adds workspace scanning to server startup; on large workspaces (10K+
-  templates) the initial scan needs streaming and progress notifications.
-  Implement with `workspace/configuration` so users can cap the scope.
-* `registerHelper`-style host-defined helpers remain unreachable until the
-  registry abstraction in ADR-018 grows an editor-visible projection.
-* User-defined inline partials in non-FullBars dialects are unreachable as
-  written — RawBars/MaxBars do not have `{{#*inline}}`. Either the partial
-  registry is host-provided (unindexable today) or partials become a
-  filesystem convention (one `.fullbars` file per partial name).
-
-== Status
-
-Proposed 2026-06-04. Implementation is gated on a small `tokenize`-based
-scanner; no language-level changes are required.

-= ADR-028 — Full LSP intelligence in hybrid host+FlatBars templates
-:adr-id: 0028
-:status: Proposed
-:date: 2026-06-04
-
-== Context
-
-xref:adr-0017-editor-support-lsp.adoc[ADR-017] amended on 2026-06-04 added an
-injection grammar (`editors/flatbars-injection.tmLanguage.json`) so a hybrid
-file like `test.java.xbars` — opened as `java` via `files.associations` —
-gets Java syntax highlighting from the host grammar AND FlatBars tag
-highlighting layered on top via the injection. Hybrid templates work for
-*syntax highlighting* immediately, with zero per-file setup beyond the file
-association.
-
-What hybrid templates do NOT get is LSP intelligence on the FlatBars regions:
-the LSP attaches to the *host* language (Java's LSP), not to FlatBars. Hover,
-completion, diagnostics, the canonicalisation quick-fix, the new
-documentSymbol / foldingRange / formatting capabilities — none of these fire
-on `{{ … }}` tags in a hybrid file.
-
-The path forward is VS Code's `vscode.languages.registerEmbeddedLanguageInfoProvider`
-API (introduced 1.86) plus an `EmbeddedDocumentProvider` style scheme: extract
-the embedded FlatBars regions into a synthetic virtual document, forward LSP
-requests across the two languages, and map positions back through the
-extraction. This record proposes the design.
-
-== Decision
-
-The VS Code extension adds an `EmbeddedLanguageInfoProvider` for every host
-language listed in `editors/flatbars-injection.tmLanguage.json` `injectTo`
-(currently 26 hosts). For each FlatBars region in a hybrid file the provider
-exposes a *virtual document* the FlatBars LSP attaches to; the extension
-shims LSP requests between the user's editor (which targets the physical
-file) and the LSP (which sees the virtual file).
-
-Concretely:
-
-* **Region extraction.** A new helper in `editors/vscode/src/embedded.js`
-  scans the physical document for `{{ … }}` runs (the same regex the
-  injection grammar uses, in a JS port to keep them in lock-step). For each
-  run it records `(physicalRange, virtualOffset)`.
-* **Virtual document.** The hybrid document is reflected at a `flatbars-embedded:`
-  URI; its content is ` `-padded host text with the FlatBars tags spliced
-  in at their original offsets so column numbers match the physical document
-  exactly. The padding glyph is a non-breaking space that the FlatBars
-  tokenizer treats as content (never a tag).
-* **Request forwarding.** The extension intercepts every LSP request on the
-  physical document whose position falls inside an extracted region and
-  re-issues it against the virtual URI, then translates result ranges back.
-  Capabilities forwarded: hover, completion, codeAction, foldingRange,
-  documentSymbol, formatting. Diagnostics flow the other way — the LSP
-  publishes onto the virtual URI and the extension forwards them onto the
-  physical URI with translated ranges.
-* **Capability gating.** Requests whose position falls OUTSIDE every region
-  pass through to the host language unchanged. This is what makes "Java
-  intelligence on Java code, FlatBars intelligence on `{{ … }}` tags"
-  work simultaneously in one buffer.
-
-JetBrains follow-up: IntelliJ has an analogous concept (the LSP customization
-hook plus the `MultiHostLanguage` API). Wiring it is a separate ticket
-because the JetBrains Marketplace plugin currently consumes the LSP through
-the platform's stock client, which does not expose the multi-host hook.
-
-== Phased plan
-
-. **Phase 1 — extraction + virtual document.** Land `embedded.js` with a
-  unit test exercising every host's region extraction. No LSP wiring.
-. **Phase 2 — hover + diagnostics on virtual.** Wire the smallest pair to
-  prove the round-trip; gate behind a `flatbars.experimental.hybridLsp`
-  setting until the rough edges shake out.
-. **Phase 3 — completion + codeAction.** Adds the request types that mutate
-  the document (codeAction's `WorkspaceEdit` needs physical-URI ranges).
-. **Phase 4 — foldingRange + documentSymbol + formatting.** Same wiring as
-  Phase 3; documentSymbol's nested children need physical ranges.
-. **Phase 5 — drop the experimental gate.** Flip the default; document in
-  the editor README.
-
-Tests per phase: hybrid fixture corpus under `editors/vscode/test/embedded/`,
-one per host language, asserting position mapping in both directions
-(physical → virtual and virtual → physical).
-
-== Consequences
-
-* Unlocks every LSP capability inside hybrid templates without changing the
-  injection grammar or the LSP server. The complexity is purely
-  client-side wiring.
-* Performance: a hybrid file holds two LSP sessions simultaneously. The
-  virtual-document representation should be ephemeral (live in extension
-  memory, not the workspace) to keep watchers and indexers from doubling.
-* The padding strategy means line numbers in the virtual document always
-  match the physical document, which the LSP can stay oblivious to —
-  position translation is identity on column except across newlines. We
-  accept the small wasted bytes (` ` per host character) as the price
-  of zero column-math edge cases.
-* JetBrains side stays syntax-only until the multi-host hook ships there or
-  we add a custom integration. Communicate this in the JetBrains README so
-  Ultimate users aren't surprised.
-
-== Status
-
-Proposed 2026-06-04. Implementation gated on
-`vscode.languages.registerEmbeddedLanguageInfoProvider` (1.86+) and a small
-client-side region extractor; no engine or LSP server changes are required.
