-= ADR-0029: i18n via a host-plugged `t` (translate) operation, not bundled CLDR
-:navtitle: ADR-029 i18n helper
-:hbs: Handlebars
-
-*Status:* Accepted — *implemented* 2026-06-05 (the blessed `t` prelude operation, interpreter +
-compiled runtime; the FlatBars Lab demonstrates the seam via native `Intl` — see the amendments). *Date:*
-2026-06-05. Builds on
-xref:adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker.adoc[ADR-001] (helpers are the meaning plug-in; the core stays
-meaning-free), reuses the IoC callback shape of
-xref:adr-0022-analyse-mode.adoc[ADR-022] (truthiness is a per-engine lambda the host plugs in, seeded into
-both interpreter and compiled runtime, *no per-file config, no baked data*), extends the user-extension
-path of xref:adr-0018-user-defined-helpers.adoc[ADR-018] (`registerHelper`), and is gated by the
-compile ≡ interpret invariant of xref:adr-0011-compile-to-js.adoc[ADR-011]. It respects the dialect-purity
-boundaries of xref:adr-0007-minbars.adoc[ADR-007] (MinBars is *Mustache*) and
-xref:adr-0009-fullbars.adoc[ADR-009] (FullBars is *Handlebars-faithful*), using the engine-level opt-in
-precedent of xref:adr-0015-set-delimiters.adoc[ADR-015] (set-delimiters is a MinBars-only knob, not a
-global). Escaping follows xref:adr-0002-escaping-and-value-policy.adoc[ADR-002].
-
-== Context
-
-The https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_of_web_template_engines[Wikipedia comparison of web template
-engines] scores FlatBars *i18n: No*. The evidence is direct: the 90-operation prelude
-(`FullBars.preludeSchema`) ships no `t` / `translate` / `gettext`. Two facts frame the decision:
-
-* *This is the company we keep.* {hbs} and Mustache *also* have no built-in i18n — their ecosystems do it
-  with userland helpers/lambdas (i18next, `handlebars-i18n`, Mustache lambdas). So "absent from the core"
-  is not anomalous; the gap is a *workflow/DX* gap, not a correctness gap.
-* *i18n is meaning, and meaning is plugged in, not built in (ADR-001).* Real localization is not string
-  substitution: it needs *pluralization* (CLDR gives Polish/Arabic/Russian 3–6 plural categories),
-  *gender/select*, and locale-aware *number/date* formatting (ICU MessageFormat is the de-facto standard).
-  A naive key-lookup `t` produces grammatically wrong output for most languages — *worse* than nothing,
-  because it looks finished.
-
-Three hard constraints fell out of team review (debate recorded against this ADR):
-
-. *No CLDR/ICU data in our core or runtime.* The compiled runtime (`flatbars-runtime.mjs`) and the
-  committed Lab bundle are size-gated; CLDR plural data is tens of KB and would tax *every* compiled
-  template, including the majority that never localize.
-. *The prelude is one shared schema across all four dialects.* Adding `t` to the base prelude adds it to
-  *MinBars* (breaking the "pure Mustache" claim, ADR-007) and *FullBars* (Handlebars ships no `t`,
-  ADR-009) — a faithfulness regression even though byte-identical conformance would stay green (the spec
-  corpora never call `t`).
-. *Whatever ships must satisfy compile ≡ interpret (ADR-011)* or `test:compile` goes red.
-
-== Decision
-
-Adopt the truthiness pattern (ADR-022) for localization: *FlatBars supplies the call site; the host
-supplies the brain; we never bundle CLDR.*
-
-. *`t` is a blessed operation in the shared kernel prelude* (`Kernel.Prelude`), reserved for the
-  *core-surface family* — *RawBars, FullBars, and MaxBars* — and *absent from MinBars* (the separate
-  Mustache peer engine has its own closed prelude, so adding to the kernel prelude never touches it; ADR-007
-  stays intact). *RawBars is included precisely because it is the desugared core surface* (not a
-  meaning-free substrate): FullBars's `pass:[{{t …}}]` desugars to a core `t` operation, so the operation
-  *must* exist at the RawBars level for the desugar target to be complete, and RawBars runs the same
-  prelude/engine. As implemented, the prelude `t` ships only the *fallback* (return the key unchanged); it
-  carries no locale or CLDR data. Because — like every prelude operation — `t` only fires when applied with
-  arguments (`pass:[{{t "k"}}]`), a bare `pass:[{{t}}]` still reads the data field `t`, so nothing is
-  shadowed.
-
-. *The host supplies the brain by registering `t`* (the IoC seam of ADR-018), not via a separate callback
-  parameter: the interpreter's `renderWith` helper bag and the compiled runtime's `rt.register("t", fn)`
-  both shadow the prelude fallback. The registered function receives the *message key* and the *named
-  arguments* (the `key=value` hash as a trailing dict) and closes over the locale (e.g.
-  `pass:[(key, args) => translate(locale, key, args)]`). The host owns the catalog, locale resolution, and
-  all CLDR/ICU behaviour (plurals, select, gender, number/date) — typically its existing i18n library, or
-  the browser's native `Intl` (see the 2026-06-05 amendment). *FlatBars ships no plural rules and no CLDR
-  data.* Conceptually this is the truthiness pattern (ADR-022) — a host-plugged rule, the same on both
-  interpreter and compiled paths — reusing the registration seam rather than a bespoke env field.
-
-. *Surface.* The head is `t`, the first argument is the message key, the rest are named arguments:
-+
-[source,handlebars]
-----
-{{t "cart.summary" count=cart.size name=user.name}}
-----
-+
-In MaxBars this also composes with pipes (`cart.size | t "cart.summary"` is *not* the shape; the key is
-the head argument — pipe sugar applies to value-producing operations, see xref:maxbars.adoc[]).
-+
-*Name: lowercase `t`, not `T`.* An uppercase `T` was considered for ergonomics — it reads more like a
-sigil and is harder to overlook in a dense template — and rejected. `t` is the universal i18n function
-name (i18next, gettext, Rails, Vue, react-i18next), so it is recognized on sight and lets ported templates
-work unchanged; the prelude is case-sensitive, so `T` would silently break `pass:[{{t …}}]`. It would also
-be the *only* uppercase operation among the 90 lowercase ones. Most importantly, `t` is an *operation
-name*, not a sigil (FlatBars has no keywords — "the head of an application is always a name", ADR-001);
-making it look like grammar would miscategorize it. The "don't overlook it" need is met in the *editor*
-layer instead — bold tag emphasis (ADR-026) and operation-name painting both already make `pass:[{{t …}}]`
-stand out — which is the correct place for visual salience. No `translate` alias ships (canonical-only;
-legacy spellings are a lint concern, ADR-019).
-
-. *Escaping is unchanged (ADR-002).* The callback returns a `String`; it lands *escaped* in
-  `pass:[{{t …}}]` and *raw* in `pass:[{{{t …}}}]`, exactly like every other helper, with `safe` as the
-  SafeString escape hatch. Messages that intentionally carry markup use the triple-stache. *No new
-  escaping axis is introduced.*
-
-. *Missing-key policy: fallback-and-flag, never throw.* With no `t` registered the prelude fallback renders
-  the key unchanged (a host that returns a marker for a missing key gets that instead), and *analyse mode*
-  (ADR-022 Part B) / the linter can flag it. A strict mode that errors on a missing key is opt-in (for CI,
-  not render). Production renders never hard-fail on one missing translation.
-
-. *compile ≡ interpret.* The prelude fallback is *pure* (return the key), so a template using `t` with no
-  host registration renders byte-identically interpreted and compiled. With a host `t`, the same registered
-  function runs on both paths (`renderWith` for the interpreter, `rt.register` for the compiled runtime).
-  `test:compile` gates the no-host case; the with-host parity is verified directly.
-
-== Consequences
-
-* The Wikipedia *i18n: No* becomes *Yes (host-plugged)* for RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars, with the honest
-  footnote that the plural/format brain is the host's — which is exactly how i18next-backed {hbs} works.
-* The catalog gains a `t` entry (`FullBars.Catalog`, the LSP `operations.json`); `npm run gen:catalog` and
-  `npm run gen:operations` regenerate them and `check:catalog` / `check:operations` gate the drift. `t` is
-  now hover-documented and operation-painted in the editors.
-* *Only MinBars is unaffected* — its separate closed prelude does not gain `t`, so ADR-007 purity and the
-  Mustache conformance claim are untouched. RawBars *does* gain `t` (ADR-008's `nonEmpty` truthiness is
-  orthogonal and unchanged); this is required, not incidental — it is the desugar target FullBars/MaxBars
-  lower to. FullBars's `t` is an *extension* beyond Handlebars (faithful to the workflow, not a Handlebars
-  built-in); `hbs-conformance` is unaffected because the corpus never calls `t`.
-* Zero bundle-size impact and no behavioural change for templates that don't localize: no CLDR ships, and a
-  bare `pass:[{{t}}]` still resolves to the data field.
-
-=== What we explicitly do NOT do
-
-* *No ICU MessageFormat engine in-core, no CLDR plural rules in our runtime* (rejected option D in the
-  debate): heavy data, violates meaning-free + the bundle gates. Plurals are the host's job.
-* *No per-file `@locale` directive.* Locale is the host's, closed over by the registered `t` — mirroring
-  ADR-022's rejection of per-file `@truthiness`.
-* *No `t` in MinBars.* It lives in the *kernel* prelude (shared by RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars), never in
-  MinBars's separate Mustache prelude — so the Mustache-purity claim stays clean without a conditional
-  mechanism (rejected option B was forcing it onto *every* engine, which would have hit MinBars).
-* *No dedicated translate-callback parameter or new env field.* The host plugs in through the existing
-  ADR-018 registration seam (`renderWith` / `rt.register`), which already marshals a host function and
-  shadows the prelude fallback — no second mechanism.
-
-== Alternatives considered (debate ratings)
-
-[cols="1,4,1"]
-|===
-| Option | Summary | Verdict
-
-| A — recipe only
-| Document `registerHelper('t', …)` + i18next; ship no engine surface. The honest "you can already do
-  this today" answer, and how {hbs}/Mustache users localize.
-| *Adopt as the interim*, but it documents a workaround rather than closing the gap.
-
-| B — `t` in the base prelude
-| Simplest, but adds `t` to MinBars + FullBars schemas.
-| Rejected — pollutes Mustache/Handlebars faithfulness.
-
-| C — opt-in module + host `translate` callback
-| This ADR. Truthiness pattern applied to localization; no CLDR shipped; dialect-gated.
-| *Accepted (proposed).*
-
-| D — full ICU/CLDR in-core
-| Correct plurals out of the box, but tens of KB of data in core/runtime.
-| Rejected — violates meaning-free + bundle gates.
-
-| E — `number` / `date` / `selectPlural` (+ `relative`) helpers
-| A locale-aware formatting helper set, same host-register discipline.
-| *Adopted* — all are blessed prelude operations alongside `t` (pure fallbacks: plain text; the English
-  one/other rule; "N units ago"). All four accept an Intl options hash — the trailing dict passes through
-  with no arity change (the fallbacks ignore it; the host reads it).
-|===
-
-== Follow-ups
-
-. ✅ *Done — the interim recipe and Lab demo:* the `/localize` guide renders `pass:[{{t …}}]` live via the
-  host-register seam, on the browser's native `Intl` (see the 2026-06-05 amendment), gated by `check:i18n`.
-. ✅ *Done — this ADR (C):* the `t` prelude operation (RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars; not MinBars), the host
-  brain via the ADR-018 registration seam (interpreter + compiled runtime), the pure key-returning
-  fallback, catalog/operations generation, and `test:compile` parity.
-. ✅ *Done — the E formatting set:* `number` / `date` / `selectPlural` / `relative` are blessed prelude
-  operations alongside `t` (pure fallbacks — plain text, the English one/other rule, and "N units ago" —
-  overridden by the host's native `Intl`). All four read an Intl options hash
-  (`pass:[{{number n style="currency" currency="EUR"}}]`, `pass:[{{selectPlural n type="ordinal"}}]`,
-  `pass:[{{relative v u numeric="always"}}]`), which the trailing dict delivers without an arity change.
-. *Conformance note:* add an `i18n` row to xref:fullbars-compat.adoc[] documenting that the `t` operation
-  (shared by RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars) is an *extension* beyond Handlebars (faithful to the workflow, not a
-  Handlebars built-in), the same framing ADR-018 used for `registerHelper`.
-
-== Amendment (2026-06-05): the Lab demonstrates the seam via native `Intl` — i18next is not vendored

-it, the way the Lab vendors `jsonata` (`lab/vendor/jsonata.mjs`, ~78 KB) for the data-shaping guide. Team
-review (debate recorded against this ADR) rejected vendoring and adopted *option C+*: the Lab demonstrates
-the i18n integration *seam* using the browser's native `Intl`, with i18next available only as an
-*unbundled* documented escape hatch.
-
-Decision and rationale:
-
-. *No i18next in the bundle.* The browser already ships the CLDR brain — `Intl.PluralRules` (every
-  language's plural categories), `Intl.NumberFormat`, `Intl.DateTimeFormat` — at *zero* bytes. JSONata
-  earned its vendor because data-shaping-before-render has no platform equivalent; i18n's plural/format
-  machinery *is* the platform, so vendoring i18next would be redundant weight plus a version/CVE pin and an
-  ecosystem blessing. The Lab vendors a library only when the platform can't already do the job.
-
-. *Demonstrate the seam, framed as Lab-as-host.* A live card (`tutorials/src/components/TryI18n.jsx`,
-  sibling of `TryJsonata.jsx`) and a `/localize` guide wire a `t` helper to native `Intl` via the existing
-  `registerHelper` / `renderWith` path (ADR-018) — *not* a new engine feature. This *reinforces* the
-  ADR's "i18n is the host's job" thesis (the Lab is acting as the host) rather than implying FlatBars does
-  i18n; the page says so explicitly.

-= ADR-0030: symbolic analyse mode, coverage honesty, and the host `PathSchema` seam
-:navtitle: ADR-030 symbolic analyse
-
-*Status:* Accepted — *implemented* 2026-06-06. Extends xref:adr-0022-analyse-mode.adoc[ADR-022] (analyse
-mode, the data-driven truthiness portability check): same `Decision` trace, same named-rule menu, same
-`reportMarkdown`/`findings`/`jsonataScaffold` outputs. Reuses the host-pluggable-callback pattern of
-xref:adr-0022-analyse-mode.adoc[ADR-022] (`Truthy`) and xref:adr-0029-i18n-helper.adoc[ADR-029]
-(`Translator`) for the new `PathSchema` seam. Respects the meaning-free thesis of
-xref:adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker.adoc[ADR-001]: no schema is baked; the host plugs it in.
-
-== Context
-
-Analyse mode (ADR-022 Part B) renders a template against *real data* and observes every truthiness
-decision the engine made, flagging the ambiguous four (`0` `""` `[]` `{}`) when a named rule would branch
-the other way. It is genuinely useful — but it has one structural weakness that a team review surfaced:
-
-* *It only sees what the sample data exercises.* The report literally says "_no portability findings — for
-  that data_". A green run on `{ "count": 5 }` says nothing about `count: 0`. "No findings" reads as "safe"
-  but proves only "safe for this one sample" — a footgun.
-* *The fix can't be "provide better data".* Hand-crafting adversarial data for every path does not scale, and
-  the engine has no schema to reason about which values a path can hold (ADR-001: types are a host concern).
-
-The goal is to decouple *coverage* from the data sample without baking a type system into the meaning-free
-core, and to make "no findings" honest about its scope.
-
-== Decision
-
-. *Symbolic what-if (potential findings).* For every condition whose *observed* value is **not** one of the
-  ambiguous four and not always-falsy (`false`/`null`), derive the *same-type* ambiguous value — a number ⇒
-  `0`, a non-empty string ⇒ `""`, a non-empty array ⇒ `[]`, a non-empty object ⇒ `{}` — and emit a
-  **potential finding** ("`count` (observed `5`) would diverge if it ever holds `0`"). This is a pure
-  post-process over the recorded `Decision`s — no extra render, no new wrapper — so its output is a function
-  of the *template*, not the sample, which is what CI wants to gate. A *bare-path* condition carries its
-  data path and JSONata fix; a *computed* condition (`pass:[{{#if (and a b)}}]`) gets the same type-based
-  potential finding without a targetable path (the generation half of the review's #1/#5, unified).
-
-. *Coverage honesty.* Every `Finding` gains a `kind` (`"observed"` vs `"potential"`), and `reportMarkdown`
-  states what it checked: _N conditions evaluated · M observed · K potential_, with potential findings in
-  their own clearly-hypothetical section ("_would diverge if …_"). "No observed findings" can no longer be
-  misread as "portable for all data".
-
-. *Optional host `PathSchema` seam.* A host may plug in `PathSchema = String -> Value -> Boolean`
-  ("could this path hold this value?") — seeded exactly like `Truthy` (ADR-022) and `Translator`
-  (ADR-029), **not** baked. A potential finding for path `p` and ambiguous value `av` is suppressed when
-  `schema p av == false` (the host's types rule it out: "`count` is always a present positive number").
-  Default is `\_ _ -> true` (no schema ⇒ every what-if stands), so it costs nothing when unused and never
-  violates the meaning-free core.
-
-. *Data-access misses as an advisory finding.* Analyse also wraps `lookup`, recording bare paths that
-  resolve to absent/`null`. These surface as `kind: "miss"` findings ("`user.naem` resolved to null for this
-  data — likely a typo"), the highest-signal typo catcher we have. Like every data-observed signal they are
-  *advisory* and carry the same coverage caveat ("for this data").
-
-. *Lint stays static; analyse owns data + symbolic.* The split from the review holds: `flatbars lint`
-  remains static, value-free, and CI-gating (aliases, scoped variables, i18n usage); analyse owns everything
-  data- or symbolic-driven and stays *advisory* — observed/miss findings depend on the sample, and only the
-  symbolic *potential* findings (a function of the template) are stable enough to gate. They cross-link, they
-  do not merge.
-
-== Consequences
-
-* The facade `analyze(template, data)` returns observed **and** potential **and** miss findings (each tagged
-  `kind`), and the report leads with the coverage line. `analyzeWith(schema, template, data)` adds the host
-  `PathSchema`. The Lab Truthiness panel groups by `kind`; `/analyse` teaches "observed vs potential".
-* The named-rule machinery, the `recoverPath`/`fixFor`/`describe` helpers, and `jsonataScaffold` are reused
-  unchanged — potential findings emit the same JSONata cleanup for their (hypothetical) path.
-* No new render pass: symbolic findings are derived from the existing `Decision` trace, so analyse stays a
-  single pure render (`WriterT (Array Decision) (Either Error)`), no `Effect`/`Aff`.
-* The `PathSchema` seam is the third instance of the same pattern (truthiness, i18n, now schema) — the host
-  supplies meaning, the core stays meaning-free.

-= ADR-0031: migrate the spec site from Antora (AsciiDoc) to Astro Starlight (MDX)
-:navtitle: ADR-031 spec site → Starlight
-
-*Status:* Accepted — 2026-06-06. A documentation-toolchain decision; it touches no
-engine semantics. The de-risk spike succeeded and was carried to a full build: a
-Markdown twin of the helper catalog, a reproducible AsciiDoc→MDX converter, and the
-*entire* 45-page spec (31 ADRs included) now build in Astro Starlight with Pagefind
-search and `starlight-links-validator` reporting every internal link valid. That
-green build validates the decision, so it is Accepted. Owner: Werner. Honours the
-design-system single-source-of-truth contracts of
-xref:adr-0017-editor-support-lsp.adoc[ADR-017] (tokens, vocabulary, one wordmark) and
-keeps the spec as the contract the packages target
-(xref:adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker.adoc[ADR-001]).
-
-*Implementation status.* The migration is *additive*: the Starlight site
-(`spec/`) is built and green, while Antora remains the live spec. Two steps remain
-before the destructive cutover (retiring Antora), deliberately not rushed: (1) a
-*content-fidelity pass* over the auto-converted MDX — AsciiDoc description lists,
-the one PlantUML diagram (→ Mermaid), and callout markers — so the converted
-contract reads as well as the source; and (2) the *cutover* itself — delete
-`docs/` + `antora-playbook.yml`, retire the one-time converter, and repoint the
-four `docs/`-reading gates (`check:catalog`, `check:tokens`, `check:adr-nav`,
-`check:glossary`). Keeping the authoritative AsciiDoc source until the fidelity
-pass is complete is what avoids locking conversion artefacts into the contract.
-
-== Context
-
-The normative spec in `docs/` is the contract the PureScript packages target — 46
-AsciiDoc pages (≈7,360 lines), of which 31 are ADRs, built today by Antora
-(`npm run docs`). Antora has served well but carries friction this project keeps
-hitting:
-
-* *It builds from git HEAD, so a linked worktree cannot build it in place* — a
-  recurring footgun for a repo that uses worktrees.
-* *AsciiDoc cannot import the live engine.* The learner site (`tutorials/`, Astro 6 +
-  Preact) renders *real* engine output inline by importing `lab/vendor/flatbars-engine.mjs`;
-  the spec cannot, so every example in the contract is hand-transcribed rather than
-  machine-rendered.
-* *Search needs a bolt-on extension*, and the UI comes from a remote `ui-bundle.zip`
-  pinned at HEAD rather than from the project's own design system.
-
-A team review weighed three options — stay on Antora, adopt Docusaurus, or adopt
-Astro Starlight. Docusaurus was rejected: it is a *third* rendering stack (React)
-alongside the existing Astro/Preact, which would fork the shared wordmark and token
-layer (xref:adr-0017-editor-support-lsp.adoc[ADR-017]) and duplicate the base-path /
-Lab-origin machinery the tutorials build already solves. Starlight wins on stack
-unity (same Astro family, reuses the design system and the Preact islands), built-in
-offline Pagefind search, and a direct path to live engine panes in the spec.
-
-The cost is real and was measured, not assumed: *1,223* `pass:[{{]` openers (MDX
-treats `pass:[{{]` and `<` as expression/JSX syntax — most sit inside source blocks,
-which become MDX-exempt fenced code, leaving a small prose-brace audit), and *353*
-`xref:` cross-references whose build-time integrity guarantee must be reconstructed,
-since MDX has none natively.
-
-== Decision
-
-Migrate the spec — and only the spec — to Astro Starlight, as follows.
-
-. *Target = Astro Starlight (MDX).* Same stack family as the tutorials; built-in
-  offline Pagefind; reuses the design system; avoids a third framework.
-
-. *Standalone app, not folded into `tutorials/`.* The spec ships as its own
-  Starlight project under `/spec`, linked to/from the tutorials via the existing
-  `PUBLIC_SPEC_BASE` seam — which already separates the two surfaces across several
-  pages. Isolating the contract's build keeps a careless tutorial edit from
-  red-building the spec's deploy. Shared look-and-feel comes from a factored
-  `shared/` module (wordmark, tokens, base-path/Lab helpers), *not* a merged build.
-
-. *Big-bang cutover.* One branch, one reviewable diff, one merge; rollback is a
-  revert while `docs/` stays intact until the final step.
-
-. *Versioning snapshots essential releases only.* The `starlight-versions` plugin,
-  triggered on tagged spec releases (first `0.1.0`), bounded to avoid folder-snapshot
-  bloat. HEAD is "current".
-
-. *All 31 ADRs convert; flat `adr/*.mdx`, status in frontmatter, grouped only in the
-  sidebar.* Status changes over an ADR's life; its URL must not, so status never
-  enters the path.
-
-. *Route `/spec`, dropping Antora's redundant component segment* (`/flatbars/spec/<page>`,
-  not `…/spec/flatbars/<page>`). A redirect map plus a new `check:redirects` gate keep
-  old URLs and in-repo `.adoc` links resolving — link stability is gated, not hoped.
-
-. *Build-time guarantees are reconstructed, not dropped.* `starlight-links-validator`
-  (build-failing) replaces Antora's `xref` integrity; `astro check` + `astro build`
-  replace the AsciiDoc parse gate; a `check:mdx-braces` lint fails on unescaped
-  `pass:[{{]`/`<` outside fences.
-
-. *ADR-031 is recorded "Proposed" first and flipped to "Accepted" only after a
-  de-risk spike* proves the three unknowns together: the catalog Markdown emitter, a
-  representative page conversion (`concepts`), and one working live engine pane.
-
-== Alternatives considered
-
-*Docusaurus v3* was the other serious MDX candidate and is rejected. Its pitch rests
-on three claims that do not survive contact with this project's scope: (1) *stateful
-SPA interactivity* for "AST parsing labs" — but the interactive surfaces (`lab/`,
-framework-neutral HTML/JS/WASM on its own origin; the Preact islands in `tutorials/`)
-are *not* part of the spec and do not migrate, and Astro's islands architecture
-ships interactive components fine while emitting zero JS for the prose that dominates
-a contract document; (2) *native versioning* — genuinely more mature than Starlight's
-`starlight-versions` plugin, but down-weighted because this ADR snapshots essential
-releases only (D4), and both use the same folder-snapshot model; and (3)
-*future-proofing via Rspack + maintainer backing* — Rspack speeds builds, not the
-runtime payload Starlight already wins, and "institutional backing" is symmetric (Astro
-is a funded project with a first-party docs product). Decisively, Docusaurus is a
-*React* stack — a third frontend framework beside Astro/Preact — which would fork the
-design-system single-sources of xref:adr-0017-editor-support-lsp.adoc[ADR-017] (tokens,
-vocabulary, one wordmark) and duplicate the base-path / Lab-origin machinery the
-tutorials build already owns. Stack unity, less shipped JS for a prose spec, and design-system
-reuse outweigh Docusaurus's lone real edge in versioning maturity.
-
-== Consequences
-
-* *The codegen single-sources are preserved, not broken.* `FullBars.Catalog` gains a
-  `helperCatalogMarkdown` emitter beside the AsciiDoc one (same `preludeSchema`
-  source), so `check:catalog` stays a gate on the MDX partial. `gen:tokens` writes the
-  shared token CSS once for both sites; `check:adr-nav` and `check:glossary` repoint to
-  the MDX sources. The design-system invariants of
-  xref:adr-0017-editor-support-lsp.adoc[ADR-017] survive intact.
-
-* *Scope is fenced.* The `tutorials/` site is *not* migrated: its 10 pages are
-  component-dominant interactive apps (live analyse panes, galleries, JSONata fixers),
-  not prose, and stay bespoke `.astro` + Preact. "Starlight everywhere" is rejected —
-  format follows content shape. Mermaid diagrams and a broad live-pane rollout are
-  out of migration scope (the mechanism is proven once in the spike; rollout is a
-  follow-up).
-
-* *A new capability is unlocked:* the spec can render real engine output inline, the
-  same way the tutorials do, closing the hand-transcription gap.
-
-* *`CLAUDE.md` is updated as part of the cutover* — its Antora-specific guidance
-  (`npm run docs`, the playbook, `supplemental-ui`, the worktree-HEAD caveat) is
-  rewritten for the Starlight toolchain.
-
-* *Follow-ups, tracked separately:* unified cross-site Pagefind search; promoting
-  `shared/` to a real `@flatbars/design-system` workspace package; the Mermaid
-  dialect-ladder diagram; the live-pane content rollout.

-= Final ADR review (2026-06-01)
-:navtitle: Final ADR review
-
-A cross-cutting review of the whole ADR set (xref:adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker.adoc[001]–xref:adr-0013-labelled-loops.adoc[013])
-once they were drafted together. The goal was not to re-approve each record but to find the *seams
-between* them — the places where two ADRs are individually true and jointly misleading. Same cast as
-the ADR-001 review. Suggestions rated 1–5 (5 = adopt now).
-
-[NOTE]
-====
-*Post-review status (2026-06-01).* Several rating-5 items below were actioned in the same pass:
-the two extension axes are now named in xref:adr-0004-token-lexer-and-grammar-seams.adoc[];
-superset-vs-isolation is sharpened in xref:adr-0003-strict-layering.adoc[]/xref:adr-0005-dialect-ladder.adoc[];
-the engine-conformance checklist landed in xref:host-api.adoc[] §7.7; the "FullBars" term is split in
-xref:adr-0008-rawbars.adoc[]/xref:adr-0009-fullbars.adoc[] and the RawBars docstring fixed; the
-directives decision is recorded in xref:adr-0010-header-directives.adoc[] and the `mustache` alias added
-to xref:directives.adoc[]. *Still open (code, not docs):* the recursion guard
-(xref:adr-0012-recursion-budget.adoc[]), the two regression tests, and the loop-variable warn-always
-change.
-====
-
-== The tensions found
-
-=== 1. Two different "extension points" wear one word
-
-*Devi:* "ADR-004 warns that a third *grammar seam* would be a smell, then ADR-007 cheerfully adds new
-*sigils*. A reader will think MinBars is the forbidden third seam. It isn't — there are *two
-orthogonal axes* and we never named them. Axis A is the **grammar seam**: `parseExpr`/`parseHead`,
-how a dialect parses a tag *interior* (`Parser.purs:57`). Axis B is the **shape gate**: `extras` and
-the MinBars sigils, which *tag shapes* a dialect admits (`Parser.purs:271`). Adding sigils grows axis
-B and is fine; adding a third grammar seam grows axis A and is the smell."
-
-*Mara:* "Agreed, and this is the deeper point behind ADR-001's reword. The parser is *name*-agnostic
-(axis-free), *shape-aware* and *shape-gated* (axis B), and *grammar-pluggable* (axis A). Three
-sentences, three mechanisms. Right now ADR-004 blurs A and B in one 'Watch' note."
-
-*Consensus:* name the two axes explicitly in ADR-004 and cross-link ADR-007's sigils to axis B.
-*Rating 5.*
-
-=== 2. "RawBars ⊂ FullBars ⊂ MaxBars" vs. "no dialect imports another"
-
-*Petra:* "ADR-003 says dialects never import each other; ADR-005 says `maxbars → fullbars` is fine.
-Both are in the record, a click apart. That looks like the dogma cracked."
-
-*Kai:* "It didn't crack — it was never about imports. `⊂` is a *surface-superset* claim: every MaxBars
-template that avoids operators is a FullBars template. Package isolation is a *different* property,
-and RawBars *does* have it (FullBars-free closure, ADR-003). MaxBars deliberately trades isolation for
-reuse because it genuinely *is* a superset. The fix is wording: say 'no dialect imports another
-*except along the ladder's superset edge*,' and state plainly that `⊂` ≠ isolation."
-
-*Soren:* "Then make it falsifiable: a test asserting RawBars' closure excludes `fullbars`, so the one
-allowed exception can't quietly become two."
-
-*Consensus:* reword both ADRs to separate *superset* from *isolation*; add the closure test.
-*Rating 5.*
-
-=== 3. The conformance checklist is promised in three ADRs and exists in none
-
-*Soren:* "ADR-001 promised an engine-conformance checklist. ADR-002 leans on it for safety. ADR-007
-needs it to even define what 'MinBars conforms' means. It is load-bearing in three records and
-written in zero files. We are accumulating an IOU."
-
-*Devi:* "It's small, though — escape fn, stringify, truthiness default, raw-output stance, sigil set,
-real-AST-shape-or-none. That's a table in `host-api.adoc`, not a research project."
-
-*Mara:* "Build it now, precisely because three ADRs depend on it. An undefined contract is worse than

-
-*Consensus:* write the checklist into xref:host-api.adoc[] before MinBars starts. *Rating 5.*
-
-=== 4. Does MinBars retro-justify or violate ADR-003's "extract lazily"?
-
-*Mara:* "ADR-007 forces *new* kernel features — a per-engine truthiness default, a recursion guard.
-ADR-003 said extract lazily. Is MinBars making us extract *eagerly* for a thing that isn't built?"

-already has two consumers the moment MinBars needs `mustache` while the others need `handlebars` —
-that *is* the second consumer. Same for the recursion guard: it hardens the reference `partialH`
-*today* (`Prelude.purs:501` is unbounded) and serves MinBars tomorrow. These are textbook lazy

-
-*Devi:* "One caveat — do them as *P0 shared prereqs* (ADR-007's own phase plan) and keep them green

-=== 5. The loop-variable lint only fires with a schema

-templates have no schema. That's the majority case going unguarded for a footgun we *introduced* by
-dropping `@`."

-= The core model
-:navtitle: The core model
-
-FlatBars rests on a few decisions. Every later rule is a consequence of them.
-
-== 0. Two phases: a skeleton, then a walk
-
-The core is a *parser*. Its entire output is a *skeleton AST* — a uniform tree of `Content`,
-`Output`, and `Block` nodes (xref:evaluation.adoc[]). The parser attaches *no meaning*: it does not
-know what any identifier does, does not know which identifiers are "helpers," does not know `else`,
-and performs no checks beyond "is this well-formed structure."
-
-Meaning is a *second pass*: a *walk* over the skeleton, supplied by the engine you build. The walk
-validates the tree against the engine's rules and interprets it — precisely the relationship
-between a JSON document and a JSON Schema. FlatBars defines the tree and the walking contract; the
-engine defines the schema and the interpreter.
-
-Everything below describes the interpretation of the reference engine, *FullBars*. A different engine may choose
-differently; the core does not care.
-
-== 1. Everything is an operation
-
-A template is a sequence of *content* and *outputs*. An output evaluates one expression and writes
-its value. The only compound expression is an *operation* — an *application* of a name. (At the host
-API this same thing is called a *helper*, the term {hbs} uses; the xref:concepts.adoc#glossary[glossary]
-pairs the native words with that synonym, and xref:host-api.adoc[] keeps it.)
-
-[source,text]
-----
-{{{city}}}                          <1>
-{{{lookup this "city"}}}            <2>
-{{{upcase (lookup this "name")}}}   <3>
-----
-<1> Calls the operation `city` with no arguments. Not a variable, not `this.city`.
-<2> Reads the `city` field of the current context, by calling the operations `lookup` and `this`.
-<3> `upcase` applied to one argument — the grouped sub-application `(lookup this "name")`.
-
-There are *no variables*. The parser sees `city` as an identifier at the head of an application; the
-engine resolves it in the *environment* and invokes it. And there is no logic-less core for an operation
-to be an *escape hatch from* — application *is* the language — so an operation is not a "helper" in the
-subordinate, auxiliary sense the word carries elsewhere; it is the primary thing.
-
-== 2. Application is juxtaposition; parentheses are grouping
-
-`head arg1 arg2` applies. Parentheses do not mean "call"; they *group* a multi-token application so
-it fits a single argument slot. A whole top-level expression therefore needs *no* parentheses:
-
-[source,text]
-----
-{{{lookup this "age"}}}             top-level application — no parens
-{{{upcase (lookup this "name")}}}   upcase of ONE argument (the group)
-{{{upcase lookup this "name"}}}     WRONG: upcase applied to THREE arguments
-----

-notation where every call is parenthesized. The only parentheses you ever write group a nested
-application that sits in argument position.
-

-The operator position holds an *identifier*, never a computed value. Nothing in the language
-produces a callable value, so nothing else can sit there. This is enforced syntactically for blocks
-(the closing `pass:[{{/name}}]` must repeat the name) and is what keeps a `Value` free of functions
-(xref:evaluation.adoc[]). Higher-order use goes through a helper such as `apply`.

-Because a bare name is a helper call, *scoped state is just scoped helpers*. A block helper such as
-`each` installs nullary helpers (`index`, `first`, the item context `this`, …) for the duration of
-its body, then removes them.

-= Header directives (`@trim`) and the truthiness model
-:hbs: Handlebars
-
-A *directive* is a `@key`/`@key: value` marker carried in a short `pass:[{{! … }}]`
-comment at the **head** of a file. The core lifts directives meaning-free (the
-`Sep` precedent applied to comments — xref:grammar.adoc[]); the engine assigns
-meaning. Because carriage lives in the core parser, every dialect (RawBars,
-FullBars, MaxBars) inherits directives uniformly.
-
-== The mechanism
-
-[source,handlebars]
-----
-{{! @trim: none }}
-Hello {{ name }}!
-----
-
-Rules (xref:lexical.adoc[]):
-
-* Directives live **only** in short `pass:[{{! … }}]` comments. A long
-  `pass:[{{!-- … --}}]` comment is inert prose — so JSDoc `@param`, e-mail
-  handles, etc. are safe by construction.
-* The parser keys on `@<key>` heads (`[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*`); a value runs to
-  the next head or the block end, trimmed. A bare `@key` (no colon) is a flag
-  (`= @key:true`). Layout is free; canonical style is one `@key:value` per line.
-* **Header-only.** Directives are recognised before the first non-comment tag.
-  Leading content/whitespace does not close the header — only a real tag does. A
-  directive after that point is a `DirectiveAfterHeader` parse error.
-* Unknown keys are **carried but lint-warned** (forward compatibility), not an
-  error.
-
-== Truthiness — a fixed per-engine rule (ADR-022)
-
-[IMPORTANT]
-====
-*The per-file `pass:[{{! @truthiness: … }}]` directive was removed* — see
-xref:adr-0022-analyse-mode.adoc[ADR-022]. Truthiness is now each engine's *one fixed rule*: **FullBars**
-uses `handlebars` (Handlebars fidelity), **RawBars** and **MaxBars** use `nonEmpty`, **MinBars** uses
-`mustache`. (The dialects therefore *diverge* in value policy — RawBars/MaxBars are not Handlebars clones.)
-There is no per-file override, no per-partial scoping, and no alias/shape-list value to write. A leftover
-`@truthiness` directive in an old template is *inert* — carried, never an error, but **lint-warned as
-deprecated** so a stale directive does not silently mislead. The model below describes those fixed rules
-and how to write *portable* templates; the analyse mode (ADR-022 Part B) checks portability against real
-data.
-====
-
-Each engine's rule decides which value *shapes* `if`/`unless`/`and`/`or`/`not` (and MaxBars' `&&`/`||`/`!`)
-treat as false. The named rules — the menu engines are built from — are:
-
-[cols="1,2,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Rule |Falsy set |Notes
-
-|`handlebars` |`false null "" 0 []` |*FullBars*; `pass:[{}]` truthy, `"0"` truthy
-|`nonEmpty` |`false null "" [] {}` |*RawBars/MaxBars*; truthy ⟺ non-empty present value — `0` truthy (use `val > 0`), every empty container falsy
-|`mustache` |`false null []` |*MinBars*; `0`/`""`/`pass:[{}]` truthy
-|`minimal` |`false null` |comparison only (analyse): only `false`/`null` false
-|`presence` |`false null [] {}` |comparison only (analyse): present ⇒ truthy; matches *StringTemplate4* (see below)
-|===
-
-Decisions worth stating: `"0"` is truthy under every rule; `0` is falsy only under `handlebars`; `pass:[{}]`
-is falsy under `nonEmpty`/`presence`; `""` is falsy under `handlebars`/`nonEmpty`; `NaN` is always truthy;
-`safe ""` is falsy iff `""` is in the rule (content-based — xref:fullbars-compat.adoc[] §1.4).
-
-`includeZero` on a single `if`/`unless` makes the number `0` truthy *for that one test* — genuine
-Handlebars compat, but a Handlebars-only escape hatch (not portable). It is a per-call helper option, no
-longer tied to any falsy-set machinery.
-
-=== Where other engines sit
-
-Each named rule is some real engine's rule — which is why they are the useful targets for a *portable*
-template, and the set the analyse mode replays to detect divergence.
-
-[cols="1,2,2",options="header"]
-|===
-|Engine |Falsy set |FlatBars rule
-
-|{hbs} (default) |`false null "" 0 []` |`handlebars`
-|Mustache |`false null []` |`mustache`
-|Ruby / Lua / Lisp `nil` |`false null` |`minimal`
-|*StringTemplate4* |`false null [] {}` |`presence`
-|===
-
-*StringTemplate4* (Parr's ST4) tests a conditional with `Interpreter.testAttributeTrue`:
-`null` and `Boolean false` are false; an empty `Collection`/`Map`/`Iterator` is
-false; **every other non-null object — including `pass:[""]` and `0` — is true**
-("it's present"). That is exactly `presence`. ST4 thus disagrees with {hbs} on
-`pass:[""]`/`0` (truthy in ST4, falsy in {hbs}) and with Mustache on `pass:[{}]`
-(falsy in ST4, truthy in Mustache).
-
-=== The portable core
-
-Reading the table by *shape* rather than by engine isolates what is safe to lean
-on across engines:
-
-* **Always falsy** (every rule): `false`, `null`.
-* **Always truthy** (every rule): a non-empty string, a non-zero number, a
-  non-empty array, a non-empty object, and `NaN`.
-* **Engine-dependent — the ambiguous four:** `pass:[""]`, `0`, `pass:[[]]`,
-  `pass:[{}]`. No two of the mainstream engines agree on all four (`""`/`0`:
-  falsy in {hbs}, truthy elsewhere; `pass:[[]]`: falsy everywhere except
-  `minimal`; `pass:[{}]`: falsy only in `presence`/ST4).
-
-A template that must render identically under more than one engine should
-therefore **never put one of the ambiguous four in a boolean position.** Branch
-on them *explicitly* instead — `pass:[{{#each xs}}…{{else}}…{{/each}}]` for a
-"non-empty list" (it renders `else` on empty on every engine), an explicit
-`pass:[{{#if (eq s "")}}]` for "blank" — so the decision no longer rides on the
-host's truthiness rule. FlatBars cannot prove this statically (it has no value
-types — a name's runtime shape is unknown at parse time), so the guarantee is
-checked *against real data* by the analyse mode
-(xref:adr-0022-analyse-mode.adoc[ADR-022]): `pass:[flatbars analyse <template>
-<data.json>]` reports every condition that would branch differently on another
-engine, with a fix each, and `--emit-jsonata` emits a reviewable data-cleanup
-scaffold.
-

-
-`@trim: standalone | none` toggles Handlebars-style standalone-line trimming: a
-line holding only a block open/close or a comment has its indentation and
-trailing newline removed. **On by default.** This is the one directive the *core*
-itself acts on, because whitespace is syntactic (the core already owns `~`).
-
-Output tags (`pass:[{{ }}]` / `pass:[{{{ }}}]`) and bare `pass:[{{else}}]`
-separators are never standalone-trimmed. Explicit `~` composes on top.

-Precedence (highest first): the `@trim` directive, the CLI `--trim standalone|none`,
-a `flatbars.json` `pass:[{ "trim": "standalone" | "none" }]` in the working
-directory, then the built-in default (on).
-
-== Compilation
-
-Both interpreter and compiler honour `@trim` identically. Truthiness is a
-*callback* in both: the compiled module seeds its root frame with the engine's
-truthiness callback — `rt.truthyHandlebars` (FullBars), `rt.truthyNonEmpty`
-(RawBars/MaxBars), or `rt.truthyMustache` (MinBars) — so a compiled template
-branches under the same rule as the interpreter, asserted byte-for-byte by the
-conformance harness (xref:adr-0022-analyse-mode.adoc[ADR-022]).

-Errors fall in two phases. *Structural* errors come from the core parser: the bytes are not a
-well-formed skeleton. *Validation* errors come from the engine walk: the skeleton is well-formed but
-violates the engine's schema (an unknown helper, a bad arity, an illegal clause). The split mirrors

-== 4.1 Structural (parse) errors — raised by the core
-
-[cols="1,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Error |Cause
-
-|`UnterminatedTag` |an opener with no matching closer before end of input
-|`UnterminatedComment` |`pass:[{{!--]` with no `pass:[--}}]`
-|`UnterminatedRaw` |`pass:[{{{{#name}}}}]` with no `pass:[{{{{/name}}}}]`
-|`MismatchedBlock` |`pass:[{{/a}}]` closing a `pass:[{{#b}}]`
-|`HeadNotIdent` |a group or literal in *head* position — a block/close/separator head must be an `Ident` (e.g. `pass:[{{#42}}]`). A bare literal in *output* position, `pass:[{{42}}]`, is allowed (it emits like `pass:[{{{42}}}]`).
-|`EmptyOutput` |`pass:[{{{}}}]` with no expression
-|`BadEscape` |an invalid string escape inside a `STRING`
-|===
-

-`else`. `pass:[{{else}}…]` is just a block; if it appears where the engine does not expect
-a clause, that is a *validation* error (4.2), not a parse error. Every structural error carries a
-source offset (`parseErrorOffset`) pointing at the offending tag — an unclosed/mismatched block
-points at its *opener*. Given the source, `parseErrorAt src pe` returns the 1-based
-`{ line, column, offset, message }` (via `Span.lineColumn`), and `renderParseErrorAt src pe` formats
-it as `pass:[line:column: message]` for a host to print.
-
-== 4.2 Validation errors — raised by the engine walk
-
-[cols="1,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Error |Cause
-
-|`UnknownHelper name` |`name` is not defined in any helper frame
-|`ArityError` |a helper received the wrong number of arguments
-|`TypeError` |a helper received an argument of the wrong shape
-|`ClauseError` |a block contains a separator the helper does not accept, or in an illegal order
-|`HelperError` |any other failure a helper chooses to raise

-*separate up-front pass* over the whole `Template` (rejecting a template before any output, the way
-a schema validator rejects a document) or *lazily* during rendering. The reference engine, *FullBars*, validates

-reports every violation with its source span.

-(`pass:[{{{lookup this "nope"}}}]`) is *not* an error in the reference engine — `lookup` returns

-= 3. The skeleton AST & the walk
-:navtitle: 3. AST & the walk
-
-Phase 1 (the core) produces the *skeleton AST* defined here. Phase 2 (an engine you supply) *walks*
-it to validate and render. This chapter gives the AST and the value type normatively, then specifies
-the *walk contract* the reference engine, *FullBars*, implements.
-
-== 3.1 The skeleton AST (normative)
-
-[source,haskell]
-----
-type Template = Array Node
-type Span     = { start :: Int, end :: Int }   -- code-unit offsets of the opening tag
-
-data Node
-  = Content  String
-  | Output   Span Expr                       -- span, expression
-  | Block    Span Ident (Array Expr) Template -- span, head, args, body (one sub-tree)
-  | RawBlock Span Ident (Array Expr) String   -- span, head, args, verbatim body
-  | Sep      Span Ident (Array Expr)          -- span, head, args (a separator marker)
-
-data Expr
-  = Lit Value          -- only Str / Num arrive from the parser
-  | App Ident (Array Expr)
-----
-
-Every tag-level node carries the source `Span` of its opening tag, for diagnostics; `Content` does
-not (it is literal text). `Span.lineColumn` turns an offset into a 1-based line/column.
-
-There is no comment node (the lexer drops them), no inverse field on `Block` (branching uses `Sep`
-markers; xref:grammar.adoc[]), and no `Group` constructor — parentheses affect *parsing* only, so
-`(e)` and `e` produce the same `Expr`. *This tree carries no meaning.* `App "if" […]` and
-`Sep "else" []` are just identifiers and arguments; whether `if` exists, what it does, and whether
-`else` splits it are all Phase-2 questions.
-
-== 3.2 The value type (normative)
-
-[source,haskell]
-----
-data Value
-  = VString  String
-  | VNumber  Number
-  | VBool    Boolean
-  | VNull
-  | VArray   (Array Value)
-  | VObject  (Map String Value)
-  | VSafe    String          -- a string already safe to emit unescaped (see 3.6)
-----
-
-[IMPORTANT]
-====
-`Value` has *no function case*. Helpers are not values; they live in the engine's environment under
-names and can never be produced, stored, or passed by the language — the direct consequence of "the
-head of an application is always a name" (xref:concepts.adoc[]). Values stay serializable and
-comparable; higher-order behaviour goes through a helper such as `apply`.
-====
-
-`VSafe` is the only non-data case and exists solely at the output boundary; see 3.6.
-
-== 3.3 The walk contract
-
-An *engine* is anything that turns a `Template` and some data into output. The contract is one
-function:
-
-[source,haskell]
-----
-runTemplate :: forall m env. Monad m => Engine m env -> Template -> m String
-----
-
-The driver is *polymorphic* in the result monad `m` (a pure host uses `Either Error`; an async one
-`ExceptT Error Aff`, under `MonadThrow Error m`) and in the environment type `env`. `env` is the
-engine's business; the reference engine uses a frame stack (as a newtype, `RefEnv m`, so the
-recursive `RefEnv → Helper → Ctl → RefEnv` is well-founded):
-
-[source,haskell]
-----
-newtype RefEnv m = RefEnv
-  { helpers :: List (Map Ident (Helper m (RefEnv m)))   -- a stack of frames; head is innermost
-  , context :: Value                                    -- what `this` returns
-  }
-----
-
-* `helpers` is a *stack of frames*. Resolution searches innermost-outward; first match wins. A block
-  helper pushes a frame for its body and pops it — the whole of "scope" (xref:concepts.adoc[]).
-* `context` is the current data, reached only via `this`. `with`/`each` push a frame *and* set a new
-  `context`.
-
-== 3.4 Validation is part of the walk
-
-Before (or as) it interprets a node, the walk *validates* it against the engine's rules — exactly
-like checking a JSON document against a JSON Schema:
-
-* `App name` — is `name` a registered helper? (else `UnknownHelper`)
-* arity — did `name` get the argument count it requires? (`ArityError`)
-* argument shape — are the values the right kind? (`TypeError`)
-* block shape — are this block's separators (`else`, `case`, …) ones this helper allows, in a
-  legal arrangement? (`ClauseError`)

-The *core does none of this*. A conforming engine MAY validate the whole tree up front (a static
-pass, like schema validation) or lazily as it renders; the reference engine validates lazily. See
-xref:errors.adoc[].
-
-== 3.5 The reference walk
-
-[source,text]
-----
-render env (Content s)            = s
-render env (Output e)             = stringify (eval env e)
-render env (Block name args body) = stringify (apply (resolve env name)
-                                                      (ctl env body)             -- Ctl handle
-                                                      [ eval env a | a <- args ])
-render env (RawBlock name args r) = stringify (apply (resolve env name)
-                                                      (ctl env [Content r])
-                                                      [ eval env a | a <- args ])
-render env (Sep name args)        = render env (Output (App name args))   -- a lone separator
-                                                                          -- is just an application
-
-eval env (Lit v)         = v
-eval env (App name args) = apply (resolve env name) (ctl env []) [ eval env a | a <- args ]
-
--- ctl env children = { env, children, render, span, clause: \n -> splitClause n children }
-----
-
-Arguments are evaluated *eagerly, left to right*, before the helper runs. Block bodies are the
-exception: a helper receives its body *unevaluated* (as a `Template`) and decides what to do with it.
-
-== 3.6 Helpers and the control handle
-
-*FlatBars drives the whole walk — inversion of control.* It resolves and applies each helper,
-handing it a `Ctl`: a *control handle* whose fields are callbacks *into* FlatBars. A helper never
-traverses the tree itself; it asks FlatBars to render the sub-trees it chooses.
-
-[source,haskell]
-----
-type Ctl m env =
-  { env      :: env                          -- the current environment (the engine's type)
-  , children :: Template                     -- this block's body ([] for inline calls)
-  , span     :: Span                         -- source location of the enclosing tag
-  , eval     :: env -> Expr     -> m Value   -- FlatBars evaluates an expression for you
-  , render   :: env -> Template -> m String  -- FlatBars renders a sub-tree for you
-  , clause   :: Ident -> { before :: Template, body :: Maybe Template } }  -- split at a separator
-
-type Helper m env = Ctl m env -> Array Value -> m Value
-----
-
-An *inline* helper ignores the handle. A *block* helper uses it: it may `render` its `children` zero
-or more times, under environments it constructs (pushing scoped helpers, shifting `context`), and it
-may `clause` to split `children` at a `{{name}}` separator.
-
-[source,haskell]
-----
--- if: render the body up to the {{else}} separator; render the else clause otherwise.
-ifHelper ctl [cond] =
-  let { before, body } = ctl.clause "else"
-  in if truthy cond
-       then VSafe <$> ctl.render ctl.env before
-       else VSafe <$> ctl.render ctl.env (fromMaybe [] body)
-
--- ctl.clause "else" finds the first  Sep "else" _  in the children, returning
--- the nodes before it and the nodes after it.
-----
-
-`each` calls `ctl.render` once per element with a per-element frame (installing `index`, `first`,
-`this`, …) and uses the same `ctl.clause "else"` for an empty-collection clause. `with` shifts
-`context`. None of this is in the core — it is the reference engine's reading of the `{{else}}`
-separator.
-
-== 3.7 Stringification, escaping, and safety
-
-`stringify` converts a `Value` to output text:
-
-[cols="1,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Value |Output
-|`VString s` / `VSafe s` |`s`
-|`VNumber n` |the shortest round-tripping decimal of `n`
-|`VBool b` |`"true"` / `"false"`
-|`VNull` |the empty string
-|`VArray` / `VObject` |host-defined; the reference host joins arrays with `","` and errors on objects
-|===
-
-[IMPORTANT]
-====
-*The core never escapes.* HTML escaping is the helper `escapeHtml`, which returns a `VSafe`. The
-`VSafe` tag makes escaping *idempotent at the boundary*: a value already escaped (or deliberately
-trusted via `safe`) is not escaped again as it flows through another helper. This is the FlatBars
-analogue of {hbs}' `SafeString`, carried in the value rather than implied by which braces you typed.
-====
-
-== 3.8 Determinism
-
-Given the same template, context, starting frame, and pure helpers, the walk is deterministic and
-side-effect-free. Side effects (e.g. `log`) are confined to `M`.

-= FlatBars
-:description: A template-engine construction kit: a parser that yields a skeleton AST, plus a contract for the validating, interpreting pass an engine layers on top.
-
-[.lead]
-*FlatBars* — _bare rods_ — is not a template engine. It is the *substrate you build one on*.
-
-It is two things, and only two things:
-
-. a *parser* that turns Handlebars/Mustache-style source into a *skeleton syntax tree* — pure
-  structure, no meaning; and
-. a *contract* for the *second pass* — a validating, interpreting walk over that tree — that an
-  engine supplies on top.
-
-The split is the whole idea. Think *JSON and JSON Schema*: JSON fixes a uniform structural syntax
-and knows nothing about what any document _means_; a schema is a separate pass that decides which
-shapes are legal and what they stand for. FlatBars is the JSON; the engine you build is the schema
-plus the interpreter.
-
-== What makes it different
-
-[cols="1,3"]
-|===
-|The core has no semantics
-|The parser does not know what `if` does, whether output should be escaped, what a path is, or even
-that an identifier names a "helper." It produces `Content`, `Output`, and `Block` nodes and stops.
-All meaning is added by the xref:evaluation.adoc[engine walk].
-
-|No built-in helpers, no keywords
-|`if`, `each`, `with`, `unless`, `lookup`, HTML escaping — and `else` — are *userland*. The core
-ships none of them and reserves no names. The xref:prelude.adoc[reference engine], *FullBars*, reproduces
-{hbs}, but you can delete, replace, or rename any of it.
-
-|No sugar in the core
-|Dotted paths, `pass:[{{ }}]` auto-escaping, `@`-variables, `as \|x\|`, partials — all of that lives
-in an *optional* xref:surface.adoc[surface dialect] that compiles to the core skeleton.
-
-|Everything is a helper application
-|In the reference engine a bare identifier `pass:[{{{city}}}]` *calls the helper* `city`. To read a
-data field you call a helper: `pass:[{{{lookup this "city"}}}]`. No variables, no implicit context.
-
-|Application is juxtaposition; parens group
-|`pass:[{{{upcase (lookup this "name")}}}]` is `upcase` applied to one argument; the parentheses
-*group* the nested application. The {hbs} subexpression model, used uniformly — not Lisp prefix.
-
-|`Value` is pure data
-|A value is a string, number, boolean, null, array, or object. *Never a function.* Values stay
-serializable; helpers live in a separate, scoped environment.
-|===
-
-== The two phases
-
-[plantuml,phases,svg,opts=inline]
-....
-@startuml
-skinparam shadowing false
-skinparam rectangle { BorderColor #1f1d1b FontName monospace }
-rectangle "Surface dialect (optional sugar)\n{{name}}  a.b.c  @index  ../x  as |x|  {{> p}}" as S #fdf0e6
-rectangle "PHASE 1 — FlatBars core\nlex + parse -> skeleton AST\n{{{ }}}   {{# }}   {{{{# }}}}   comments   ~\nstructure only; no meaning, no else, no keywords" as C #f5f3f0
-rectangle "PHASE 2 — the engine walk (you supply)\nvalidate + interpret the AST, like a JSON Schema\nhelpers, arity, truthiness, escaping, clauses (else/case/...)" as P #e9f5ee
-S --> C : desugars to
-C --> P : handed to
-@enduml
-....
-
-The xref:concepts.adoc[core model] explains the decisions. The
-xref:appendix-handlebars.adoc[appendix] maps *every* {hbs} concept onto FlatBars with no gaps.
-
-[NOTE]
-====
-This document specifies the *core* (Phase 1) normatively, and the *contract* a Phase-2 engine must
-satisfy. The xref:prelude.adoc[reference engine] and xref:host-api.adoc[host API] are one
-conforming implementation, in PureScript. Code fragments use `text`/`haskell` blocks and are
-normative only where marked _normative_.
-====
-
-== The reference dialect: FullBars
-
-The engine and surface dialect that ship with FlatBars are *FullBars* — a member of the
-Handlebars/Mustache family, familiar on sight, but a *dialect* with its own reasoned choices, not a
-clone: a helper-first core, escaping as an explicit helper, `pass:[{{else}}]` as a name-agnostic
-separator, a native short-circuit `pass:[{{elif}}]`, content-based safe-string truthiness, and
-explicit (`~`) whitespace. The differences from {hbs} are *features, not gaps* — see
-xref:fullbars-compat.adoc[the FullBars dialect — differences from Handlebars]. And because the core
-reserves no names, you can delete, replace, or rename any of it and grow a different dialect on the
-same substrate.

-= 1. Lexical structure
-:navtitle: 1. Lexical structure
-
-This chapter defines how a template's bytes are split into *content* and *tags*, and how the pieces
-inside a tag are tokenized. The grammar in xref:grammar.adoc[] consumes these tokens to build the
-skeleton AST. Nothing here knows what any identifier *means*.
-
-== 1.1 Source
-
-A template is a sequence of Unicode characters; the host decodes bytes to text first. The lexer
-recognizes a small set of *tag openers* and treats everything else as literal *content*.
-
-== 1.2 Tag openers and the brace count
-
-[cols="1,2,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Opener |Closer |Meaning
-
-|`pass:[{{{]`  |`pass:[}}}]`   |*Output* — evaluate one expression, write its value. The only inline output form.
-|`pass:[{{#]`  |`pass:[}}]` … `pass:[{{/name}}]` |*Block* — a named application that also captures one sub-template (its body).
-|`pass:[{{#>]` |`pass:[}}]` … `pass:[{{/name}}]` |*Partial block* — a `PartialBlock`-sigil block over a clean partial-name head. Opt-in via `ParseOptions.partialBlocks`.
-|`pass:[{{#*]` |`pass:[}}]` … `pass:[{{/name}}]` |*Decorator* — a `Decorator`-sigil block over a clean decorator-name head (e.g. `pass:[{{#*inline}}]`). Opt-in via `ParseOptions.decorators`.
-|`pass:[{{!]`  |`pass:[}}]`    |*Short comment* — discarded. May not contain `pass:[}}]`.
-|`pass:[{{!--]`|`pass:[--}}]`  |*Long comment* — discarded. May contain `pass:[}}]`, `pass:[{{]`, and `--`.
-|`pass:[{{{{#]`|`pass:[}}}}]` … `pass:[{{{{/name}}}}]` |*Raw block* — body captured verbatim, never tokenized.
-|`pass:[{{]` _Ident_ `pass:[}}]`| |*Separator* — the bare double-stash `pass:[{{ name args }}]`. A flat marker; the lexer reads the *shape*, never the name.
-|===
-
-That is the entire opener set. `pass:[{{#]` is the general block *opener* (`pass:[{{#>]` and
-`pass:[{{#*]` are its two opt-in specialisations); the bare double-stash
-`pass:[{{ … }}]` is a *separator*, recognized by shape. There is deliberately no:
-
-* `pass:[{{^}}]` inverse opener — "render when falsy" is the `unless` helper, not a syntax.
-* escaped-output `pass:[{{ }}]` *in the core* — the double-stash is a separator here; escaping is the
-  helper `escapeHtml`. The xref:surface.adoc[surface dialect] reuses `pass:[{{ E }}]` for escaped
-  output, desugaring it to `pass:[{{{ escapeHtml … }}}]`; the two layers read it differently.
-
-The separator's identifier — `else`, `elif`, `case`, `default` — is *opaque to the lexer and parser*
-(xref:grammar.adoc[] §2.4). The lexer matches the *longest opener*: `pass:[{{{{]` before
-`pass:[{{{]` before `pass:[{{#*]` / `pass:[{{#>]` before `pass:[{{#]` before a bare `pass:[{{]`, and
-`pass:[{{!--]` before `pass:[{{!]`.
-
-== 1.3 Content and brace escaping
-
-Any run of characters not beginning a tag is *content*, emitted verbatim. A backslash immediately
-before a tag opener escapes it: the opener is emitted literally and the backslash is consumed.
-
-[source,text]
-----
-\{{{x}}}      emits the literal text {{{x}}}
-\{{x}}        emits the literal text {{x}}      (a bare {{ is a separator opener)
-\\{{{x}}}     emits a literal backslash, then evaluates {{{x}}}
-----
-
-[IMPORTANT]
-====
-*`pass:[{{]` is significant.* Because the bare double-stash is a separator opener (§1.2), a literal
-`pass:[{{]` in content must be written `pass:[\{{]`. For blocks of text full of braces, a raw block
-(`pass:[{{{{#raw}}}}…{{{{/raw}}}}]`, §1.7) is cleaner. This is a deliberate change from earlier
-drafts, where `pass:[{{ }}]` was not part of the core at all (xref:adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker.adoc[ADR-001]).
-====
-
-== 1.4 Whitespace control: `~`
-
-A tilde immediately inside a tag opener or before a tag closer trims *all* contiguous whitespace on
-that side of the tag, including newlines.
-
-[source,text]
-----
-{{{~ x ~}}}                    trims around this output
-{{~#each xs~}}…{{~/each~}}      trims around the block tags
-----
-
-`~` is resolved entirely in the lexer: it adjusts the adjacent content runs and disappears. It never
-reaches the AST, so it is not sugar — there is nothing to desugar.
-
-[IMPORTANT]
-====
-FlatBars performs *no implicit "standalone" whitespace removal*. {hb} silently strips the line
-around a block/partial/comment that stands alone; FlatBars does not. Whitespace is removed only where
-you write `~`. Predictable and explicit; see xref:appendix-handlebars.adoc#comments-raw-ws[A.7].
-====
-
-== 1.5 Tokens inside a tag
-
-Within `pass:[{{{ … }}}]`, `pass:[{{# … }}]`, and the head of a raw block, the lexer produces:
-
-[cols="1,3,2",options="header"]
-|===
-|Token |Definition |Examples
-
-|`IDENT`
-|An identifier. One or more characters from `A`–`Z`, `a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `_`, `-`, `+`, `*`, `?`, `!`,
-`/`, `.`, `<`, `>`, `=` that does not parse as a `NUMBER`. Must not start with a digit, `-`+digit,
-`"`, `(`, `)`, or whitespace.
-|`each`  `escapeHtml`  `partial-block`  `>`  `eq`
-
-|`STRING`
-|`"` … `"` or `'` … `'` with escapes `\\` `\"` `\'` `\n` `\t` `\r`. May contain spaces and any
-tag-like text; the lexer does not look inside strings.
-|`"home town"`  `'pro'`
-
-|`NUMBER`
-|Optional `-`, decimal digits, optional fraction. No exponents in v1.
-|`3`  `-2.5`  `0`
-
-|`LPAREN` `RPAREN`
-|`(` and `)` — grouping.
-|`(` `)`
-
-|whitespace
-|Insignificant inside a tag (significant only via `~`).
-|
-|===
-
-The permissive `IDENT` set lets names like `>` (partial), `eq`, `+`, and `partial-block` be
-written. `.` is a legal `IDENT` character, so `a.b` lexes as a *single* identifier — the core never
-splits it. Dotted *paths* are a surface concept (xref:surface.adoc[]).
-
-== 1.6 Comments
-
-[source,text]
-----
-{{! stripped, no }} allowed inside }}
-{{!-- stripped; may contain }} and {{ and -- dashes --}}
-----
-
-Both forms are discarded during lexing and never appear in the AST.
-
-== 1.7 Raw blocks
-
-[source,text]
-----
-{{{{#raw}}}}
-Hello {{name}} — emitted verbatim.
-{{{{/raw}}}}
-----
-
-After the `pass:[}}}}]` closing the raw-block head, the lexer captures everything up to the matching
-`pass:[{{{{/IDENT}}}}]` as one uninterpreted string. The closing `IDENT` must equal the opening one.
-
-== 1.8 Lexer summary (informative)
-
-[source,text]
-----
-CONTENT  --"\\" + opener-->  emit literal opener, stay in CONTENT
-CONTENT  --opener-->         switch to matching TAG / RAW / COMMENT state
-TAG      --"~"-->            mark trim, continue
-TAG      --tokens-->         IDENT | STRING | NUMBER | ( | )
-TAG      --closer-->         back to CONTENT (apply pending trims)
-RAW      --scan-->           capture verbatim until {{{{/name}}}}
-COMMENT  --scan-->           discard until }} (short) or --}} (long)
-----

-= 6. The reference engine (prelude)
-:navtitle: 6. The reference engine
-
-The *reference engine*, *FullBars*, is a Phase-2 walk (xref:evaluation.adoc[]) plus a set of helpers that,
-together with the xref:surface.adoc[surface dialect], reproduces {hb}. *None of it is in the core.*
-It is a library you register into the helper environment. Delete `each` and `pass:[{{#each}}]` stops
-validating; the core is unaffected. Rename `escapeHtml` and update your Surface. This is what "no
-built-in helpers, no keywords" buys you.
-
-Helper signatures use the shapes from xref:evaluation.adoc[]: a helper is `Ctl m env -> Array Value
--> m Value`; a block helper uses the control handle's `children`/`clause`/`render` and may split its
-`children` at a `{{name}}` separator via `splitClause`.
-
-== 6.1 Context and access
-
-[cols="1,1,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Helper |Arity |Behaviour
-
-|`this` |0 |Returns the current `context`.
-|`root` |0 |Returns the top-level context. Installed by the host at the outermost frame.
-|`parent` |0 or 1 |`(parent)` returns the enclosing block's context; `(parent (parent))` walks two
-levels. Installed by block helpers that shift context.
-|`lookup` |≥1 |`(lookup obj k1 k2 …)` indexes `obj` by each segment (string key or numeric index),
-returning `VNull` at the first miss. `(lookup obj)` is `obj`.
-|`true` `false` `null` |0 |The literal values `VBool true`, `VBool false`, `VNull`.
-|===
-
-== 6.2 Output and safety
-
-[cols="1,1,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Helper |Arity |Behaviour
-
-|`escapeHtml` |1 |HTML-escapes the stringified argument (`&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`) and returns a
-`VSafe`. Idempotent on `VSafe` input.
-|`safe` |1 |Marks the stringified argument as `VSafe` *without* escaping — the explicit "trust this
-markup" helper. The analogue of `new Handlebars.SafeString(…)`.
-|`json` |1–2 |Serializes the first argument as JSON *text*, returned as a plain `VString` — so surface
-`pass:[{{ json x }}]` HTML-escapes it and `pass:[{{{ json x }}}]` emits it raw (e.g. inline `<script>`
-data). Objects/arrays are first-class; integral numbers print without a trailing `.0`; object keys
-come out in key order. Compact by default; an optional options object opts into two-space
-pretty-printing — `pass:[{{ json x pretty=true }}]` (empty objects/arrays stay inline).
-|`escapeJson` |1–2 |The JSON analogue of `escapeHtml`: serializes to JSON *and* HTML-escapes, returning
-`VSafe`. For embedding JSON safely in HTML (e.g. an attribute). `escapeHtml` is idempotent on the
-result, so surface escaping never doubles up. Accepts the same `pass:[pretty=true]` option.
-|`raw` |block |A raw-block helper returning its captured body verbatim.
-|===
-
-== 6.3 Conditionals (clause-reading block helpers)
-
-[cols="1,1,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Helper |Form |Behaviour
-
-|`if` |block |`splitClauses` over its body: renders the nodes before the first separator when the
-argument is truthy; otherwise walks the `pass:[{{elif cond}}]` clauses in order, rendering the first
-whose `cond` is truthy (evaluated lazily via `Ctl.eval`, so later conditions short-circuit), and
-falls back to a terminal `pass:[{{else}}]`.
-|`elif` |1 |A *separator* the enclosing `if` interprets — `pass:[{{#if a}}…{{elif b}}…{{/if}}]`.
-Rendered standalone it is inert (returns `""`), exactly like `else`.
-|`unless` |block |The inverse of `if` (a single `pass:[{{else}}]`, no `elif`).
-|===
-
-`if`, `elif`, and `unless` *define* the meaning of nested `pass:[{{else}}…]` / `pass:[{{elif}}…]`;
-the core does not — they are ordinary separators. `if` rejects a malformed chain up front (a clause
-other than `elif`/`else`, or anything after `else`) as a `ClauseError`, so the error never depends on
-which branch the data takes.
-*Truthiness* is the *engine's* rule (a `Value -> Boolean` callback the conditionals test through;
-xref:adr-0022-analyse-mode.adoc[ADR-022]), so it depends on the dialect: **FullBars** uses `handlebars`
-(`false`/`null`/`0`/`""`/`[]` falsy; `pass:[{}]` and non-zero/non-empty truthy), **RawBars/MaxBars** use
-`nonEmpty` (`false`/`null`/`""`/`[]`/`pass:[{}]` falsy — `0` truthy), **MinBars** uses `mustache`. The
-`includeZero` option makes the number `0` truthy for one `if`/`unless` test — `pass:[{{#if n (dict
-"includeZero" true)}}]` — which matters under `handlebars` (a no-op under `nonEmpty`, where `0` is
-already truthy).
-
-== 6.4 Iteration and context shift
-
-[cols="1,1,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Helper |Form |Behaviour
-
-|`each` |block |Iterates an array or object. Per element it pushes a frame, sets `context` to the
-element, and installs scoped helpers `index` (0-based), `key`, `first`, `last`, `parent`. Optional
-binding-name arguments rename the element and index. On an *empty* collection it renders the
-`else` clause (via `splitClause "else"`).
-|`with` |block |Pushes a frame, sets `context` to its argument, installs `parent`, renders the body.
-On a falsy/absent argument it renders the `else` clause. An optional binding-name argument also
-installs the shifted context under that name.
-|===
-
-Scoped helpers installed by `each`:
-
-[cols="1,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Helper |Value inside the body
-|`this` |the current element
-|`index` |0-based position (number)
-|`key` |property name (objects) or numeric index as string (arrays)
-|`first` / `last` |`VBool` — first / last element?
-|`parent` |the collection's enclosing context
-|`parent-index` / `parent-key` / `parent-first` / `parent-last` |the *enclosing* loop's
-`index`/`key`/`first`/`last` — the target of surface `pass:[{{@../index}}]` etc. (one `../` level).
-Installed by `each`/`with` only when an enclosing loop provided them.
-|===
-
-== 6.5 Composition / data helpers
-
-[cols="1,1,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Helper |Arity |Behaviour
-
-|`dict` |even ≥0 |`(dict "k1" v1 …)` builds a `VObject`. Target of the hash desugaring (5.4).
-|`apply` |≥1 |`(apply name args…)` — the higher-order escape hatch: `name` is a `VString` naming a
-helper, applied to the remaining arguments. How a "helper held in data" is called, since values are
-never functions.
-|`log` |≥1 |Emits its arguments to the host log (an effect in `M`) and returns `VNull`.
-|===
-
-== 6.6 Partials
-
-[cols="1,1,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Helper |Form |Behaviour
-
-|`partial` |2–3 |`(partial name ctx hash?)` renders the registered partial `name` with `context = ctx`,
-the optional `hash` object merged onto it. *As a block* (`pass:[{{#partial name}}body{{/partial}}]`)
-the body is the fallback (rendered if `name` is unregistered) and is exposed inside the partial as the

-Target of `pass:[{{> @partial-block}}]`.
-|===
-
-== 6.7 A minimal engine is enough
-
-You do not need all of the above. A static-site author might register only `this`, `lookup`,
-`escapeHtml`, `if`, and `each`; a configuration templater only `lookup`, `eq`, and `or`. The engine —
-the helpers *and* the clause vocabulary they read — is the product surface you design. The core never
-presumes which of these exist.
-
-== 6.8 Helper catalog (generated)
-
-The table below is *generated* from `FullBars.preludeSchema` — the same single source the validator
-uses (`FullBars.Catalog.helperCatalogAdoc`; regenerate with `npm run gen:catalog`, checked in CI by
-`npm run check:catalog`). It is the authoritative list of names, arities, block-ness, and one-line
-*descriptions*; each description is the operation's own `doc` (the same string the editor shows on

-*Source* is `registered` for helpers with a runtime in `prelude` and `scoped` for variables a block
-helper installs (`root`/`parent`/`index`/`key`/`first`/`last`/`partial-block`).
-
