-spelling; the inline-partial *decorator* `pass:[{{#*inline "name"}}…{{/inline}}]`
-is the *required* FullBars author form and desugars internally to the core
-`inline` helper. The core lexes `pass:[{{#>]` and `pass:[{{#*]` as the distinct
-`PartialBlock` and `Decorator` sigils — each with a clean head (the partial name
-for `pass:[{{#>}}]`, the decorator name `inline` for `pass:[{{#*inline}}]`) and a
-`pass:[{{/…}}]` close that simply repeats that head. They are opt-in via
-`ParseOptions.partialBlocks` / `decorators` (on for FullBars; the austere dialects
-gate them off as a located `DisallowedShape`). The bare
-`pass:[{{#inline}}]` is rejected by `FullBars.checkBareInline` with a located
-`DisallowedShape` error — this gate is FullBars-surface-only (RawBars and MaxBars
-still accept bare `pass:[{{#inline}}]`). See the
-xref:fullbars-compat.adoc[compatibility matrix] for per-feature status.
-====
-
-[IMPORTANT]
-====
-*Parenthesis convention.* A top-level expression inside `pass:[{{{ }}}]` needs no grouping — it is
-already one `Expr`. Parentheses appear only around a *nested* application in argument position. So
-the desugaring of `pass:[{{ name }}]` is `pass:[{{{ escapeHtml (lookup this "name") }}}]` — `escapeHtml`
-is the top-level operator (no wrapper), and `(lookup this "name")` is parenthesized because it is an
-argument.
-====
-
-== 5.1 Output: `pass:[{{ }}]` and `pass:[{{{ }}}]`
-
-[cols="2,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Surface |Core
-
-|`pass:[{{ E }}]` |`pass:[{{{ escapeHtml E' }}}]`
-|`pass:[{{{ E }}}]` |`pass:[{{{ E' }}}]`
-|===
-
-{hbs}' ampersand form `pass:[{{& E }}]` (unescaped) is accepted as an alias of the triple-stash
-`pass:[{{{ E }}}]` (see §5.6) — both mean "do not escape". The triple-stash is the canonical FullBars
-spelling; the austere RawBars and MaxBars dialects accept only it and reject `pass:[{{&}}]`.
-
-`E'` is `E` after the *path rewrite* (5.2). If `E'` is itself a multi-token application it is wrapped
-in parentheses before being handed to `escapeHtml` (it is now an argument): `pass:[{{ upcase x }}]` →
-`pass:[{{{ escapeHtml (upcase (lookup this "x")) }}}]`.
-
-== 5.2 Paths become `lookup`
-
-[cols="2,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Surface path |Core
-
-|`name` |`(lookup this "name")`
-|`a.b.c` |`(lookup this "a" "b" "c")`
-|`a.1` or `a.[1]` |`(lookup this "a" 1)`
-|`a.[home town]` |`(lookup this "a" "home town")`
-|`a/b` (legacy slash) |`(lookup this "a" "b")`
-|`this` or `.` |`this`
-|`this.a` or `./a` |`(lookup this "a")`
-|`../a` |`(lookup (parent) "a")`
-|`../../a` |`(lookup (parent (parent)) "a")`
-|`@x` |`(x)`  (a scoped data helper — 5.5)
-|`@../x` |`(parent-x)`  (the enclosing loop's datum — 5.5)
-|===
-
-(The right-hand forms are shown parenthesized because in Surface a path almost always lands in
-*argument* position — e.g. as the argument of `escapeHtml`. When a path is the whole top-level
-expression, e.g. `pass:[{{{ name }}}]`, the desugaring is the unwrapped `pass:[{{{ lookup this "name" }}}]`.)
-
-`lookup` is *variadic*: it walks segments left to right, indexing objects by string key and arrays by
-number, returning `VNull` at the first miss. `parent` is a scoped helper that block helpers install
-to expose the enclosing context (5.5); it replaces {hbs}' implicit context stack with an explicit,
-named one.
-
-[NOTE]
-====
-A bare path `name` resolves to a *data field* (`lookup this "name"`), never to a helper, because
-Surface always wraps it. This is the opposite of the core, where `pass:[{{{name}}}]` *calls* the
-helper `name`. The two layers read the same text differently on purpose: Surface is for authors who
-think in data; the core is for the desugarer and the engine.
-====
-
-== 5.3 Helper calls, literals, and subexpressions
-
-Anything that is not a bare path is a helper call, exactly as in the core, with two literal
-conveniences:
-
-[cols="2,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Surface |Core
-
-|`true` / `false` / `null` |`(true)` / `(false)` / `(null)`
-|`(helper a b)` |unchanged — grouping is already core
-|`helper a b` (tag head) |unchanged — application is already core
-|===
-
-In *head* position a bare identifier is a helper; in *argument* position a bare identifier that is
-not a registered literal is a path. So `pass:[{{upcase name}}]` →
-`pass:[{{{ escapeHtml (upcase (lookup this "name")) }}}]`.
-
-== 5.4 Hash arguments become a trailing `dict`
-
-[cols="2,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Surface |Core
-
-|`pass:[{{helper a k1=v1 k2=v2}}]` |`pass:[{{{ escapeHtml (helper a (dict "k1" v1 "k2" v2)) }}}]`
-|`pass:[{{#helper a k=v}}…{{/helper}}]` |`pass:[{{#helper a (dict "k" v)}}…{{/helper}}]`
-|===
-
-All `key=value` pairs collapse into a single `dict` value appended *after* the positional arguments —
-the equivalent of {hbs}' `options.hash`.
-
-== 5.5 `@data` and block params become scoped helpers
-
-`each` and `with` install scoped helpers for the duration of their body; Surface `@`-variables are
-calls to them, and block params rename them:
-
-[cols="2,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Surface |Core / mechanism
-
-|`@index` `@key` `@first` `@last` |`(index)` `(key)` `(first)` `(last)` — installed by `each`
-|`@../index` `@../key` `@../first` `@../last` |`(parent-index)` … — the *enclosing* loop's datum,
-installed by `each`/`with` (one `../` level)
-|`@root` |`(root)` — installed by the host at the top frame
-|`{{#each xs as \|item i\|}}` |`{{#each xs "item" "i"}}` — `each` also installs `item` and `i`
-|`{{#with o as \|x\|}}` |`{{#with o "x"}}` — `with` installs `x` alongside the shifted `this`
-|===
-
-Renaming via `as |…|` becomes positional *binding-name* arguments to the block helper.
-
-== 5.6 Branches
-
-`pass:[{{else}}]` is already core — a separator (xref:grammar.adoc[] §2.4) — so Surface passes it
-through unchanged. Surface's only job here is the `else if` chain, which it lowers to the engine's
-flat `pass:[{{elif cond}}]` separator (the condition is still path-rewritten):
-
-[cols="2,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Surface |Core
-
-|`pass:[{{#if c}}A{{else}}B{{/if}}]` |`pass:[{{#if c}}A{{else}}B{{/if}}]`
-|`pass:[{{#each xs}}A{{else}}B{{/each}}]` |`pass:[{{#each xs}}A{{else}}B{{/each}}]`
-|`pass:[{{#if a}}A{{else if b}}B{{else}}C{{/if}}]` |`pass:[{{#if a}}A{{elif (lookup this "b")}}B{{else}}C{{/if}}]`
-|===
-
-`else`, `elif`, and `unless` are *engine* names (xref:prelude.adoc[] §6.3). A different engine could
-read a clause named `otherwise` or provide `case`/`default`; Surface simply targets whatever the
-engine defines. (Authoring `pass:[{{elif b}}]` directly in Surface also works — it is a clause
-separator like `pass:[{{else}}]`.)
-
-FullBars supports Mustache's inverted section `pass:[{{^x}}…{{/x}}]` (and the triple variant
-`pass:[{{{^x}}}…{{{/x}}}]`), desugaring it to `pass:[{{#unless x}}…{{/unless}}]` — so "render when
-falsy" reads the way Handlebars authors expect. You may always write the `unless` helper explicitly
-instead. (The austere RawBars and MaxBars dialects do *not* accept `pass:[{{^}}]` — there you write
-`unless`.) Unescaped output also has the `pass:[{{&x}}]` alias for `pass:[{{{x}}}]`.
-
-== 5.7 Partials become `partial` / `inline`
-
-[cols="2,3",options="header"]
-|===
-|Surface |Core
-
-|`pass:[{{> name}}]` |`pass:[{{{ partial "name" this }}}]`
-|`pass:[{{> name ctx}}]` |`pass:[{{{ partial "name" ctx' }}}]`
-|`pass:[{{> name k=v}}]` |`pass:[{{{ partial "name" this (dict "k" v) }}}]`
-|`pass:[{{> name ctx k=v}}]` |`pass:[{{{ partial "name" ctx' (dict "k" v) }}}]`
-|`pass:[{{> (expr)}}]` (dynamic) |`pass:[{{{ partial (expr) this }}}]`
-|`pass:[{{#partial name k=v}}body{{/partial}}]` |`pass:[{{#partial "name" this (dict "k" v)}}body{{/partial}}]`
-|`pass:[{{> @partial-block}}]` |`pass:[{{{ partial-block }}}]`
-|`pass:[{{#*inline "name"}}body{{/inline}}]` |`pass:[{{#inline "name"}}body{{/inline}}]`
-|===
-
-Block partials are written with the *core spelling* `pass:[{{#partial}}]`
-(a bare name is literalized like `pass:[{{> name}}]`) *or* the equivalent
-Handlebars *sigil* `pass:[{{#> name}}…{{/name}}]`. Inline partials use the
-Handlebars *decorator* `pass:[{{#*inline "name"}}…{{/inline}}]`, which desugars to
-the core `inline` helper; the bare `pass:[{{#inline …}}]` spelling is *rejected*
-(`DisallowedShape`) in FullBars — authors do not write `inline` bare. A block `partial`
-renders the named partial with its `body` as both the fallback (when the partial is missing) and the
-`pass:[{{> @partial-block}}]` yield point; `inline` definitions are hoisted into the registry before
-rendering.
-
-Partials render *unescaped* — a partial produces markup, not a data value, so the desugaring is the
-plain triple-stash with no `escapeHtml`. The partial *name* desugars to a `STRING` literal; a dynamic
-partial keeps the computed expression. `partial`, `inline`, and the scoped `partial-block` are engine
-helpers; see xref:appendix-handlebars.adoc#partials[A.6]. The scoped `partial-block` is also installed
-under the synonym `yield`, the hyphen-free spelling the non-Handlebars dialects use for the same yield
-(MaxBars `pass:[{{yield}}]`, RawBars `pass:[{{{yield}}}]`; see xref:maxbars.adoc[]).
-
-== 5.8 What Surface does *not* change
-
-Comments, raw blocks, whitespace `~`, and brace-escaping are *core* features and pass through
-untouched.

-# FlatBars Lab — manual smoke checklist (layer 3)
-
-The Lab's output-view system is tested in three layers (see
-`lab/output-view.mjs` and the debate that established this split):
-
-| Layer | What | Where it is checked |
-| --- | --- | --- |
-| 1 · **decision** | which pane + what text for a view | `lab/output-view.test.mjs` (pure, automated) |
-| 2 · **wiring** | tab click → correct pane visible, paint called | `lab/output-view.test.mjs` (hand-rolled fake DOM, automated) |
-| 3 · **pixels** | CodeMirror actually *renders* it, highlighted, measured | **this checklist** (manual; no headless tool asserts it honestly) |
-
-Layers 1–2 run offline in `npm run test:lab` with **zero browser dependencies**.
-Layer 3 is what a real browser — and only a real browser — can confirm. A
-headless harness (jsdom/Playwright) was deliberately *not* adopted: it would add a
-heavy/networked dependency to do, with lower fidelity, what the fake-DOM harness
-already does for wiring, while still not honestly covering pixels. Revisit
-Playwright only if visual regressions become a tracked priority, as an opt-in gate
-off the default `test:lab` path.
-
-## How to run
-
-```sh
-npm run gen:bundle          # rebuild lab/vendor/flatbars-engine.mjs if the engine changed
-python3 -m http.server -d lab 8080   # or any static server; the Lab is static files
-# open http://localhost:8080
-```
-
-The Lab imports CodeMirror from esm.sh, so this pass needs network.
-
-## Checklist — output views
-
-Load an example, then click each output-view tab. For every text view, confirm
-the read-only editor shows content with the right syntax highlighting; for the
-preview views, confirm the iframe renders.
-
-- [ ] **Plain Text** — rendered output, source-map provenance decorations on hover.
-- [ ] **HTML Preview** / **Markdown Preview** — iframe renders (text pane hidden).
-- [ ] **Render Data** — the view-model as YAML.
-- [ ] **Compiled JS** — the emitted module (FlatBars dialect), JS-highlighted.
-- [ ] **Migrated MaxBars** — the template rewritten from Handlebars to MaxBars
-      (template-grammar highlighted); residuals appear as leading `{{! … }}`
-      comments. The tab is **absent** under a non-FlatBars engine (gates on the
-      `migrate` capability). Opening `/lint`'s migrate examples via *Open in Lab*
-      lands here.
-
-## Checklist — Lint diagnostics panel (ADR-019)
-
-The canonicalization lint is a **dock panel** (next to Truthiness). With a
-template using a deprecated alias or legacy scoped variable
-(e.g. `{{ plus a b }}`, or `{{#each xs}}{{ index }}{{/each}}` in RawBars/MaxBars):
-
-- [ ] the **Lint** tab appears in the diagnostics dock, with a finding count and an
-      amber badge (green when there are none).
-- [ ] each finding row shows the offending name, the message naming the canonical
-      spelling, and `main:line:col`; clicking a row jumps to the **name** in the
-      editor (not just the tag — the location is refined to the name's offset).
-- [ ] the tab is **absent** under a non-FlatBars engine (gates on the `lint`
-      capability), and the scoped-variable lint does **not** fire in FullBars (where
-      `{{@index}}` is canonical).
-- [ ] opening `/lint`'s lint examples via *Open in Lab* lands with this panel open.
-
-## Checklist — Truthiness diagnostics panel (ADR-022)
-
-The truthiness report is a **dock panel** (next to Coverage / Data Access), not an
-output view. With a template that has an ambiguous condition over empty/zero data
-(e.g. `{{#if bio}}…{{/if}}` with `{"bio":""}`):
-
-- [ ] the **Truthiness** tab appears in the diagnostics dock, with a finding count
-      and an amber badge (green when there are none).
-- [ ] each finding row shows the tag, the value tested, the engines it flips
-      under, `main:line:col`, and a **Fix:** line.
-- [ ] clicking a row jumps to the condition in the template editor.
-- [ ] editing the data re-runs it (a finding clears when the value stops being
-      ambiguous; `0 findings — portable` shows).
-- [ ] the tab is **absent** when a non-FlatBars engine is selected (it gates on
-      the `analyse` capability).
-
-## Checklist — MinBars truthiness toggle (ADR-022 S2)
-
-Open the Lab under `?engine=minbars`. A **mustache.js truthiness** checkbox sits in
-the output toolbar (right of the focus button); it is absent under every other
-engine. With `{{#n}}has{{/n}}{{^n}}none{{/n}}` and data `{ "n": 0 }`:
-
-- [ ] unchecked (default): renders **has** — `0` is truthy (the language-agnostic
-      spec / Ruby rule).
-- [ ] checked: renders **none** — `0` is falsy (the mustache.js rule); the same
-      flips for an empty string, while `{}` stays truthy and `[]` falsy.
-- [ ] the **Compiled JS** view reflects the toggle (`rt.truthyHandlebars` when
-      checked, `rt.truthyMustache` when unchecked).
-- [ ] the choice round-trips through a share link (`#…` carries `mj:1`) and resets
-      when a catalog example is loaded.
-
-## When a view is added or changed
-
-1. Add it to `VIEW_TABS` in `lab/output-view.mjs` and give it a `viewKind`.
-2. If it paints text, add it to the text branch in `applyView` coverage (the
-   exhaustiveness test in `lab/output-view.test.mjs` will fail otherwise).
